# CI for the intentic monorepo.
#
# One workflow, one DAG, three INDEPENDENT verify groups — test-core, test-platform, test-site, plus the
# desktop jobs — each gating only the artifacts it proves. A broken group publishes nothing of its own and
# blocks nothing of anyone else's. That split is the whole reason this is one workflow rather than several:
# `needs` edges only exist inside a workflow, and those edges are what the split buys.
#
# Node + pnpm are pinned by package.json engines/packageManager and baked into ci-base, so no version appears
# here. The runner requirements — six instances, a shared /ci-cache on the same filesystem as the work dir,
# and the host Docker socket — are in docs/ci-runner.md.
#
# FIRST RUN: ci-base is the one image with a bootstrap problem, because the jobs that could build it all run
# INSIDE it — including `changes`, the job whose probe would otherwise notice it missing. On a repository that
# has never published it, push it once by hand before the first pipeline:
#   docker build -t ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest _tools/ci-base && docker push ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
# ci-desktop needs no such step and never did — its build job runs on the host runner, and the `changes` probe
# builds it when its tag is absent, so a missing ci-desktop costs one pipeline, not a maintainer. Nothing else
# here may assume an image is present merely because its Dockerfile did not change.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

# Supersede a running pipeline on a pull request; never on main, where the release job must be allowed to
# finish. This is `interruptible: true` — which every verify job carried and the release deliberately did not.
#
# The group is PER-SHA on push, so two main pipelines never share one. A shared group with
# cancel-in-progress: false does not run them side by side — the newer run sits PENDING until the older one
# finishes, which behind a release is up to two hours, and a third push cancels the pending second. Actions
# has no per-job opt-out of a workflow-level cancel, so the shape that keeps the verify jobs cancellable
# without ever queueing a main push is a group main pushes cannot collide in at all.
# Releases stay serialized — by the release job's own `concurrency: release`.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# The DEFAULT every job inherits is read-only on both counts: `packages: read` is what pulling a ghcr
# container needs, and that is all most jobs here do. The four jobs that actually push a tag name
# `packages: write` themselves. Kept read at this level deliberately — a write granted here is a write
# handed to every job in the file, including the ones that run a fork's code.
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: read

env:
  COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT: "0"
  # The two heavy stores live on the host directory the runner mounts at /ci-cache (docs/ci-runner.md), NOT in
  # an Actions cache. Both are content-addressed stores that every job reads and appends to — exactly what a
  # shared directory is for, and exactly what a per-job archive is worst at. If the mount is absent both fall
  # back to the container's own filesystem: cold, never broken.
  # pnpm ignores PNPM_STORE_PATH/PNPM_STORE_DIR, so the store is selected by --store-dir in the composite
  # action; this variable is deliberately named so it cannot be mistaken for one pnpm reads on its own.
  PNPM_STORE: /ci-cache/pnpm-store
  TURBO_CACHE_DIR: /ci-cache/turbo
  # The fleet's turbo remote cache (_tools/turbo-cache), when the repository names one: TURBO_API and TURBO_TEAM
  # are variables, TURBO_TOKEN a secret. Empty, turbo reads them as unset and uses /ci-cache/turbo alone.
  TURBO_API: ${{ vars.TURBO_API }}
  TURBO_TEAM: ${{ vars.TURBO_TEAM }}
  TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
  # CI builds the site but never deploys it, so IndexNow submission is pure waste here — it polls the LIVE site
  # for the key file (90s timeout) and then retries a 403 five times, ~2 min per build.
  INDEXNOW_ENABLED: "0"

jobs:
  # Which parts of the tree moved. Actions has no per-job `changes:` key, so the answer is computed once
  # here and downstream jobs gate on these outputs.
  #
  # Written in bash against git rather than with a marketplace action on purpose: this repo digest-pins its
  # base images and publishes with provenance, and a third-party action in the critical path of every pipeline
  # is a supply-chain surface that buys nothing a `git diff --name-only` cannot.
  changes:
    # THE FORK BOUNDARY. This repository is public and every job below runs on the self-hosted fleet, so a
    # pull request from a fork would otherwise execute a stranger's code — install lifecycle scripts, tests,
    # build scripts — on the hosts that hold the release credentials. The runners are not ephemeral, they
    # share one /ci-cache across every job including `release`, and each mounts the host docker socket, so
    # that execution is host root and a poisoned turbo entry is a supply-chain edge into a published artifact.
    # So the fleet builds ONLY branches pushed to this repository. This guard is half of that; the repo's
    # approval-for-all-outside-contributors setting is the other half, and it is not redundant — a
    # `pull_request` event runs the workflow file from the PULL REQUEST'S OWN merge ref, so a fork that edits
    # this file runs its edited copy with the line below deleted. Approval is what that case cannot get past.
    #
    # This job and `preflight` are the DAG roots; guarding both skips everything downstream, and the third
    # copy is on `e2e-hermetic`, the one job whose condition names no `needs` output. Every remaining job is
    # already unreachable on a pull request — `images`, `images-platform` and `release` require
    # `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, and the rest derive from a `changes`
    # output that is empty once this job is skipped. The workflow-policy check asserts that, so a job added
    # without a guard or without a root in its `needs` fails the check instead of silently opening this back up.
    #
    # To run CI on an outside contribution, push its branch to this repository and open the pull request from
    # there — having read the diff first.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    # IN THE CONTAINER like every job that only reads the checkout, and that placement is worth ~4.5 minutes
    # per pipeline. This used to be a host job, and a host job on these runners must first chown the whole
    # persistent workspace back from the container jobs (which run as root) before checkout can write
    # `.git/index.lock` — a ~110k-inode reclaim that measured 4+ minutes on every single pipeline. Inside the
    # container the checkout runs as root like everything else and there is nothing to reclaim. The two jobs
    # that genuinely must run on the host — ci-base and ci-desktop, which docker-build the CI images — carry
    # the reclaim step themselves, and they run only when their own Dockerfiles change.
    #
    # The cost is one more pull of an image the runner already has, and one sharper bootstrap edge: on a
    # repository that has never published ci-base, this job cannot start at all — which the header's FIRST RUN
    # hand-push already covers, and which the `missing` probe below could never fix anyway (the probe needs
    # this job running to say the image is absent).
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        # The docker socket is what `docker manifest inspect` (the `missing` probe below) talks through.
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    # Every job in this file carries a timeout, because the Actions default is 360 MINUTES. There are six
    # runner processes on one host, so an unbounded hang is a sixth of the fleet parked for six hours. The
    # heavy jobs get 60; the two that only read the checkout get 15.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      ci-base: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.ci-base }}
      ci-desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.ci-desktop }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.desktop }}
      ic: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.ic }}
      images: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.images }}
      platform: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.platform }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history: a pull request's base.sha can sit arbitrarily far back and the diff below needs it
          # present. Cheap after the first run — the workspace persists, so this is an incremental fetch.
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Keeping node_modules is per-checkout on Actions, and this job runs in every pipeline: a
          # `git clean -ffdx` here deletes the 69k-file install, the local .turbo and .image-out on whichever
          # of the six workspaces it lands on, and the next job to land there repays it as a 2-3 minute cold
          # install.
          clean: false

      # For the `missing` probe below — the CI images are private packages, so reading a manifest needs the
      # same credential pulling one does. Seconds, and this job is off the critical path: preflight starts
      # beside it, not after it. Guarded on the same branch the probe is, so the one pipeline that cannot use
      # a registry credential — a pull request from a fork, whose GITHUB_TOKEN is downgraded to read — never
      # has to present one.
      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # EVERY CONTEXT VALUE ARRIVES THROUGH THE ENVIRONMENT, none interpolated into the script. `${{ }}` inside
      # a `run:` block is textual substitution BEFORE the shell parses the line, so a value containing shell
      # syntax becomes script rather than data — `github.ref` is the one below that a person can choose the
      # text of, by naming a branch. The fork boundary means only this repository's own branches reach here, so
      # this is hardening rather than a hole; the shape is what matters, because this block is the one people
      # copy when they add a job that needs the base SHA.
      - id: filter
        shell: bash
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          BASE_PUSH: ${{ github.event.before }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            base="$BASE_PR"
          else
            base="$BASE_PUSH"
          fi
          # The zero-SHA / force-push / first-push case (no usable base — treat everything as changed rather
          # than silently skipping the jobs that decide whether anything is checked at all) now lives inside
          # affected.mjs, so the two consumers of that decision cannot disagree about it.
          #
          # THE FOUR PRODUCT TRIGGERS, COMPUTED FROM THE WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY GRAPH rather than asserted by a
          # regex over paths. affected.mjs walks every package.json's `workspace:` edges — the same graph turbo
          # reads — from the changed files up through every package that transitively depends on one, and asks
          # whether that set reaches the desktop app, the sandbox image's payload (read out of
          # prepare-image-trees.sh, so there is no second copy of that list), or the platform apps.
          #
          # It replaces five hand-written regexes, two of which rested on a claim nothing checked — that
          # `_editor` held no dependency of any image-bound package. IT WAS FALSE: the three extensions baked
          # into the image depend on @intentic/extension-ui, which re-exports @intentic/ui out of _editor/ui,
          # so every UI-kit change had been skipping the image rebuild silently. Checked against 150 commits of
          # history: the two answers differ on 88 of them, and every difference read either way is the graph
          # being right and the regex being coarse or blind.
          #
          # --explain puts the reasoning on stderr (visible in this log); stdout is job-output syntax.
          node _tools/scripts/verify/affected.mjs "$base" "$HEAD_SHA" --explain >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # THE TWO CI IMAGES, which the graph cannot answer: they are Dockerfiles for the containers the jobs
          # run in, so nothing in the workspace depends on them, and they have a SECOND trigger — the tag they
          # publish is not in the registry at all. A path filter alone answers "has this image's recipe
          # changed", and every consumer then assumes the answer to a different question — "is the image
          # there" — is yes. It was not: ci-desktop had never been published, because the only pipelines whose
          # diff touched _tools/ci-desktop were ones where ci-base failed first, and every release since died
          # in `Initialize containers` on `manifest unknown` for an image no pipeline had ever had cause to
          # build. A tag deleted from the registry reads the same way.
          #
          # Probed only on main. A pull request must not move these tags — the push step in those jobs is
          # main-only — so a missing image is not something a pull request could fix by building one it has to
          # throw away.
          missing() {
            if [ "$REF" != 'refs/heads/main' ]; then echo false; return; fi
            docker manifest inspect "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo false || echo true
          }
          any() { if [ "$1" = true ] || [ "$2" = true ]; then echo true; else echo false; fi; }
          # The path halves come from the same script, so there is one place that reads the diff.
          changed_ci_base="$(grep '^ci-base-changed=' "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
          changed_ci_desktop="$(grep '^ci-desktop-changed=' "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
          echo "ci-base=$(any "$changed_ci_base" "$(missing ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "ci-desktop=$(any "$changed_ci_desktop" "$(missing ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # The checks that read the checkout and nothing else, ahead of the install every other job starts with.
  #
  # `_tools/checks/run.mjs` is the checkout half of what the fleet runs before landing: every test file sits in
  # a type-check program, every machine-touching suite is named as one, and every package.json specifier is the
  # one pnpm-lock.yaml recorded, among nineteen others. No node_modules, seconds of actual work.
  #
  # The measurement that put it first: across 40 main pipelines, 22 verify jobs failed and 10 died on one of
  # three of these invariants — and every one of those failed AFTER a 0.6-2.0 minute frozen-lockfile install, in
  # each of the six jobs that opens with one. Seconds here replace six of those.
  #
  # THE WORKFLOW LINT RUNS HERE TOO, and it is the one thing in this job that touches the network — two pinned
  # binaries into /ci-cache, once per runner per version, ~1s warm. It sits in this job rather than in one of
  # its own on purpose: the DAG's widest wave is five against six runner processes (docs/ci-runner.md), and a
  # fourth root would spend the single slot of headroom on a check that takes a second. What it buys is the
  # class of bug this pipeline keeps producing — a workflow that stops doing something and reports success.
  preflight:
    # The second DAG root — see the fork boundary on `changes`. The verify groups and `e2e-hermetic` hang off
    # this one, so it carries the same guard rather than inheriting one.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    container:
      # Hardcoded rather than an `env` reference: workflow-level `env` is not one of the contexts available to
      # `jobs.<id>.container`, so this string is repeated per job by the language's rules, not by choice.
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Same reason as the `changes` job: this one also runs in every pipeline, and a clean checkout here
          # is a cold install charged to whichever job lands on this workspace next.
          clean: false
      # THE WORKSPACE OUTLIVES THE COMMIT: checkout here is `clean: false` (above), so a rename leaves its old
      # directories on this persistent runner — a moved package's former directory keeps its node_modules/dist
      # and no git operation will ever remove it. The layout check then fails on ghosts no commit can fix
      # (5464 tracked files all green, and still red). Prune them first; --prune deletes exactly the
      # directories the check would have named.
      #
      # INLINE HERE AND ONLY HERE: the prune's real home is the pnpm-setup composite, beside the other repairs
      # the persistent workspace needs, which is what covers verify-core and verify-platform — they run this
      # same check through `pnpm prepass` and were reddened by it (run 34046947138). This job is the one that
      # deliberately uses no composite (checkout only, no node_modules, no network), so it carries its own.
      - run: node _tools/checks/layout.mjs --prune
      # EVERY CHECK THE MANIFEST LISTS, side by side (_tools/checks/manifest.mjs says what each is for): the
      # lockfile against the manifests, every test file in a type-check program and under a budget, the workflow
      # policy (fork boundary, permission ceilings, provenance runners, tag triggers), the byte scan, the
      # daemon's structural gates, the publish set, the UI tiers and the rest. One list, read by this job, by the
      # pre-push hook and by the turn-ending check, so a check cannot again be right and unrun: five of these
      # were red for weeks inside a `pnpm check` chain that no job and no hook ran. Checkout only, no
      # node_modules, no network, under two seconds.
      #
      # `--tidy=warn` BECAUSE THIS JOB IS A DAG ROOT. Every verify group and e2e-hermetic hangs off it, so a
      # failure here does not report one problem, it HIDES the rest of the pipeline: the day this flag was added,
      # a run reddened on ghost directories, and the type error and the two broken tests underneath it were not
      # discovered until the third round of fixes. The manifest's `gate` field says which failures are worth that
      # (`code`: the tree does not work or cannot be built) and which are not (`tidy`: the tree costs its readers
      # more than it should). Tidy failures print here as warnings and are REFUSED by nightly.yml's `tidy` job,
      # which reads one commit on a GitHub-hosted runner and gates nothing at all.
      - run: node _tools/checks/run.mjs --tidy=warn
      # actionlint + zizmor over .github/ — the workflows checked by tools that parse them, rather than by the
      # line scanners the checkout gate was growing to approximate a fraction of the same ground. The script says what
      # each tool is for, why they are pinned by sha256 rather than baked into ci-base, and which findings this
      # repository suppresses on purpose (.github/zizmor.yml, each with its reason and what would retire it).
      - shell: bash
        run: bash _tools/scripts/verify/lint-workflows.sh

  # THE THINGS ABOUT THE DATABASE NO OTHER JOB CAN SEE — that the migration history is append-only, that every
  # new entry on it can apply to a database which already holds rows, and that replaying the lot produces
  # schema.prisma. check-migrations.sh carries the full account; the short version is
  # that a `challenge` column was added by editing a migration every deployed database had already applied,
  # Prisma never re-ran it, and desktop sign-in returned an unhandled 500 in production for a week while every
  # job in this file stayed green. It could not have been otherwise: every database CI builds is created FRESH
  # from that same edited file, so the fresh ones were right, the deployed one was wrong, and each was
  # perfectly consistent with itself. Only the history can say so, which is why this job reads the history.
  #
  # The rows half was added by the same lesson told the other way round: `tunnelId` arrived as ADD COLUMN NOT
  # NULL with no default — a statement Postgres runs on an empty table and refuses on a used one — so it passed
  # here, failed on the live database, and P3009'd every deploy after it until it was fixed forward by hand.
  # An empty database cannot notice the difference, and every database this job builds is empty; reading the
  # statement is the only place the difference exists before production finds it.
  #
  # A JOB OF ITS OWN rather than a step in preflight, for the two things it needs and preflight does not:
  # `fetch-depth: 0` (preflight checks out shallow — the immutability half is a diff against the merge base),
  # and a postgres to replay into. Which is also why it is not in the verify matrix: the parity half needs an
  # EMPTY, DISPOSABLE database, and every other database in this pipeline is somebody's fixture.
  #
  # `services:` rather than a docker-run against the mounted socket: a container this job started would sit on
  # the default bridge, and this job's container sits on the network Actions made for it — the runner is the
  # only thing here that can put a database and a job on the same network, and `services` is how it is asked.
  migrations:
    needs: [changes, preflight]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.outputs.platform == 'true' && needs.preflight.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    services:
      # Reachable at `postgres:5432` — the service's name on the network Actions puts both containers on, so
      # there is no port to publish and nothing on the host to collide with a developer's own compose stack.
      # The SAME pin the platform's own compose file runs (_tools/selfhost/platform/docker-compose.yml): a
      # migration replayed against a different major is a migration checked against a different database.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18.4-alpine3.24@sha256:9a8afca54e7861fd90fab5fdf4c42477a6b1cb7d293595148e674e0a3181de15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: app
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
          POSTGRES_DB: app
          # `initdb` ends by fsyncing the whole new cluster, and that is the single slowest thing this job
          # waits on. It measures a couple of seconds on an idle machine and MINUTES on these runners, where
          # six runner processes and the image builds share one disk — 2026-08-19 the container was still
          # inside that fsync when the health gate gave up, and the job died with a postgres that was
          # perfectly healthy thirty seconds later. Nothing here outlives the job (the database is created
          # empty, replayed into, and thrown away), so durability of a cluster that cannot survive its own
          # container is a cost with no buyer.
          POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: --no-sync
        # `-h 127.0.0.1`, because the socket answers too early to mean anything. During `initdb` the entrypoint
        # runs a TEMPORARY server on the unix socket alone (listen_addresses is empty) to create the database —
        # a plain `pg_isready -U app` sees THAT and reports ready, while the port this job's DATABASE_URL dials
        # is still closed. Asking over TCP is asking the question the job actually has.
        #
        # And a start period on top: with `--no-sync` the init is seconds, but a runner busy enough to have
        # caused the failure above is busy enough to be slow again, and a first-minute refusal is a database
        # still starting, not a broken one. Retries alone cannot say that — they count from the first probe.
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U app -d app -h 127.0.0.1" --health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10 --health-start-period 60s
    env:
      MIGRATION_CHECK_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app:app@postgres:5432/app
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # The immutability half diffs against the merge base, which on a pull request can sit arbitrarily far
          # back — the same reason the `changes` job takes the full history, and just as incremental after the
          # first run on a persistent workspace.
          fetch-depth: 0
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      # THE PREDECESSOR COMMIT, spelled out, because work lands on main by direct push here and not only through
      # pull requests. Left to its own default the script would compare against `origin/main` — which on a push
      # to main IS the commit being pushed, so every migration would be diffed against itself and the check
      # would pass by construction on exactly the event it exists to police. Same two-sided answer the `changes`
      # job computes, and the same zero-SHA fallback for a first push or a force-push, which has nothing behind
      # it to compare with; the script says so and still runs the half that needs no history.
      # Through the environment, for the reason the `changes` job's filter step spells out.
      - shell: bash
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          BASE_PUSH: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            base="$BASE_PR"
          else
            base="$BASE_PUSH"
          fi
          bash _tools/scripts/verify/check-migrations.sh "$base"

  # The CI job image itself. Runs only when _tools/ci-base changes — every other pipeline skips it. It cannot
  # run inside ci-base (building that is the point), so it runs on the host runner directly.
  #
  # `latest` is pushed ONLY from main: a pull request touching this dir still builds the image to prove it
  # compiles, but must not move the tag every other pipeline pulls. Consequence: a PR that needs a NEW tool in
  # the base image cannot use it until the change lands on main.
  ci-base:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.ci-base == 'true'
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # Pushes ci-base:latest, so it needs the write the workflow default withholds.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      # THE ONE THING A HOST JOB MUST DO BEFORE IT CHECKS OUT. Every container job on these runners runs as
      # root, and all of them share ONE persistent workspace per runner — so a container job's checkout leaves
      # a root-owned tree, and a job that runs on the host as the runner user cannot write `.git/index.lock`.
      # Checkout fails, then fails a second time trying to delete the tree it also cannot write. This job and
      # ci-desktop are the only Linux jobs left on the host (docker-building the CI images is why), so they are
      # the only two that pay the reclaim — and only when their own Dockerfiles change, not per pipeline.
      #
      # The runner user is in the docker group, so a throwaway root container hands the tree back without sudo.
      # This cannot be a composite action in .github/actions: those are read out of the workspace, which is the
      # very thing this step exists to make readable.
      - name: Reclaim the workspace from the container jobs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] || exit 0
          # Whichever CI image the runner already has, so this needs no registry credential and no third-party
          # image. Neither one present means no container job ever ran here, so nothing can be root-owned.
          img=$(docker image ls -q ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest)
          [ -n "$img" ] || img=$(docker image ls -q ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest)
          [ -n "$img" ] || exit 0
          docker run --rm --entrypoint chown -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/w" "$img" -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # This job needs no install, but it runs on a workspace other jobs reuse — cleaning it would charge
          # the next one a cold install. The build context is _tools/ci-base, whose tracked files checkout
          # force-updates either way.
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - run: docker build -t ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest _tools/ci-base
      - name: Push the tag (main only)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: docker push ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      - name: Explain a pull-request build
        if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'
        run: echo "pull request — image built for validation only, tag not moved"

  # ci-base plus the Rust/Tauri/NSIS toolchain, for the three jobs that compile the desktop app. Its own image
  # rather than more layers on ci-base: it is ~3.75 GB that the verify, images and release-adjacent jobs have
  # no use for.
  #
  # It rebuilds when EITHER dir changes, because its FROM is ci-base's mutable `latest` — a ci-base bump that
  # didn't rebuild this image would leave the desktop jobs on a stale base. `needs` orders it after that
  # rebuild; the `if` tolerates a pipeline where ci-base was skipped.
  #
  # When ci-base FAILS this job skips, and a skip is the one result that carries no information downstream: it
  # is what a job reports both when it had nothing to do and when its base could not be built. So every job
  # that runs in this image guards on ci-base as well as on this one. Without that second guard a ci-base that
  # built but could not push left the desktop jobs and the release running against the PREVIOUS ci-desktop —
  # green results, and a release, for a toolchain that is not the commit's. It read as an unrelated failure
  # three jobs away.
  #
  # `!cancelled()` rather than `always()`, here and on every other guard in this file. Both override the
  # default "skip me if a `needs` job was skipped", which is what these conditions need — but `always()` also
  # runs the job when the RUN ITSELF was cancelled, so superseding a pull request left this 3.75 GB image
  # build and the Rust job below still going, and a hand-cancelled main run would still have published images
  # and rolled production.
  ci-desktop:
    needs: [changes, ci-base]
    # Wrapped in ${{ }} because a bare leading `!` is a YAML tag indicator, not an operator.
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.outputs.ci-desktop == 'true' && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    timeout-minutes: 90
    # Pushes ci-desktop:latest — same reason as ci-base.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      # As in ci-base: a host job, so the workspace comes back before checkout — see there for why.
      - name: Reclaim the workspace from the container jobs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] || exit 0
          img=$(docker image ls -q ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest)
          [ -n "$img" ] || img=$(docker image ls -q ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest)
          [ -n "$img" ] || exit 0
          docker run --rm --entrypoint chown -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/w" "$img" -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # As in ci-base: nothing here reads node_modules, but cleaning the workspace costs the next job.
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - run: docker build -t ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest _tools/ci-desktop
      - name: Push the tag (main only)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: docker push ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest
      - name: Explain a pull-request build
        if: github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'
        run: echo "pull request — image built for validation only, tag not moved"

  # Build + test every product, as ONE JOB PER RELEASE GROUP rather than one job for the monorepo. A red group
  # publishes nothing of its own and blocks nothing of anyone else's — which is what makes the `needs` edges on
  # the publishing jobs below mean anything.
  #
  # COVERAGE IS UNCHANGED against the single unfiltered job, and that is checkable rather than hoped: with
  # `turbo run <task> --dry=json`, the union of these three closures plus desktop-check's is exactly the 70
  # packages the old job covered, for `typecheck` and for `build test` alike. Re-run that comparison when
  # adding a group; a package in no group is a package nothing checks, and turbo will not say so.
  #
  # The groups deliberately OVERLAP on shared packages (_sandbox contracts, _deploy resources, _tools), because
  # turbo's `pkg...` includes a package's dependencies: a shared lib break fails every dependent group, which is
  # the correct blast radius. The duplicated
  # work is a turbo cache replay off the shared /ci-cache dir, not a second build.
  # The OSS core: every npm-published package plus the sandbox image's tree.
  #
  # The two desktop packages are subtracted rather than left to fall in with the rest: the launcher UI is the
  # desktop group's leaf, desktop-check owns it, and leaving it here would mean a vue-tsc error in a Tauri
  # window still held up the sandbox images and the npm release — the same coupling one scope down.
  #
  # The platform web app is subtracted for the same reason at a bigger price tag. share-view declares it as a
  # devDependency (it compiles web's SOURCE into its own bundle via an alias), and that one edge pulled web's
  # 248-file test suite into this closure: ~13 of this job's 20 minutes, spent re-running the exact suite
  # verify-platform was executing beside it — and this job is the gate for `images` and the entire release
  # chain. The subtraction removes only web's OWN tasks from the target set; web#build still runs here as
  # share-view's `^build` dependency, which is what keeps a web source change invalidating share-view.
  # verify-platform owns web's tests; a web break still blocks the platform deploy, the artifact it can
  # actually break.
  #
  # THE SCOPE IS NO LONGER A PARTITION. There used to be three of them — @intentic, @intentic-app, @intentic-dev
  # — and each of the three verify jobs below was spelled as one of them. One repository publishing under three
  # scopes was worth less than it cost (a package's name said which job ran it and nothing else), so there is
  # now one scope and each job NAMES the set it owns. This one is everything, minus what a job below owns.
  verify-core:
    needs: preflight
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify.yml
    with:
      filters: "--filter=@intentic/*... --filter=!@intentic/desktop-app --filter=!@intentic/desktop-smoke --filter=!@intentic/web"
    secrets: inherit

  # The hosted platform — api, web, prisma, api-contract, capability-catalog, e2e — and their closure, which
  # reaches every extension, because web declares their UI bundles as workspace dependencies and compiles them
  # in. Gates images-platform, and is the only thing that does: this job alone decides whether production rolls.
  verify-platform:
    needs: preflight
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify.yml
    with:
      # @intentic/ingress rides this gate rather than only verify-core's, because this job is the one thing
      # that decides whether production rolls — and the edge is now part of what rolls. A package shipped by a
      # pipeline it is not verified by is a package that can ship broken.
      filters: "--filter=./_platform/*... --filter=@intentic/web... --filter=@intentic/api-contract... --filter=@intentic/capability-catalog... --filter=@intentic/e2e... --filter=@intentic/localhost-https... --filter=@intentic/onboarding..."
    secrets: inherit

  # THE PROVIDER CONFORMANCE GATE: every provider's REAL CLI, driven by the real adapter, against a local
  # scripted model. It is the answer to "never release a version where some provider is broken", and it is
  # separate from verify-core because it needs a provisioning verify-core does not: the provider CLIs, at the
  # versions the packs pin.
  #
  # IT GATES THE RELEASE, and it can, because it is hermetic. Every turn here talks to @intentic/fake-model on
  # loopback instead of to a vendor, so there is no token to expire, no quota to exhaust and no outage to be
  # reddened by — the failure modes that make a real-model test unfit to block a release. The tiers that DO
  # spend real tokens run nightly and alert instead (nightly.yml, provider-smoke).
  #
  # It does not stand down quietly: with the switch on and a CLI missing, the suite FAILS naming the pack, on
  # the principle that a release gate which skips itself is not a gate.
  verify-providers:
    needs: preflight
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.preflight.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    timeout-minutes: 30
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    env:
      COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT: "0"
      PNPM_STORE: /ci-cache/pnpm-store
      TURBO_CACHE_DIR: /ci-cache/turbo
      # The daemon resolves @cursor/sdk from here (cursor/cursor-sdk.ts); the pack's own prefix is not writable
      # in this container and the licence keeps it out of the image anyway.
      INTENTIC_CURSOR_SDK_DIR: /ci-cache/cursor-sdk
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      # At the PACK's pins, never `@latest`: the tier's claim is that it exercises the shipped article, and the
      # newest CLI is by definition not what the image runs. The canary that does ask for latest is nightly.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/ci/install-provider-clis.sh
      - run: pnpm e2e:providers

  # The marketing site and the content/integration libs behind it. It gates no deploy — the site publishes from
  # Cloudflare's own git integration, outside this pipeline, so nothing here can stop a bad one — which makes
  # this the pull-request gate and the `needs` a future site-deploy job would hang off.
  verify-site:
    needs: preflight
    uses: ./.github/workflows/verify.yml
    with:
      filters: "--filter=./_site/*..."
    secrets: inherit

  # The desktop app: Rust fmt/clippy/tests + the launcher UI build. Runs only when the desktop tree changes —
  # on pull requests as the gate, and on main so a broken desktop surfaces before the release cross-builds the
  # same crate. clippy compiles against real webkit2gtk, covering the Linux target; the Windows msvc target is
  # covered by that release cross-build.
  desktop-check:
    needs: [changes, preflight, ci-base, ci-desktop]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true' && needs.preflight.result == 'success' && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure' && needs.ci-desktop.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic, desktop]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    # A debug cargo build off the shared registry, not the release-profile one desktop-verify runs — 60
    # minutes was never close to binding here, and this keeps it that way.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # The registry, shared. Overriding CARGO_HOME does not hide the baked toolchain: rustup's proxies live in
      # the image's own /usr/local/cargo/bin, which is on PATH, and they find toolchains through RUSTUP_HOME.
      CARGO_HOME: /ci-cache/cargo
      # A target dir per job, never one shared: cargo holds an EXCLUSIVE file lock on a target directory for
      # the length of a build, so two jobs pointed at one directory serialize instead of running beside each
      # other. And a build's fingerprint includes the stamped version, so jobs sharing a directory invalidate
      # each other's leaf crate and each pays a fresh LTO.
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /ci-cache/desktop-check-target
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup

      # The launcher UI first: `tauri build` would run it anyway, and a Vue error is worth failing on in
      # seconds rather than after a cargo build. Through turbo rather than a bare `pnpm --filter … build`
      # because this job OWNS the desktop packages — the verify matrix subtracts them, so their build happens
      # HERE or nowhere. No separate typecheck: desktop-app's build IS `vue-tsc --noEmit && vite build`.
      - run: pnpm turbo run build test --filter=@intentic/desktop-app... --filter=@intentic/desktop-smoke... --continue=dependencies-successful
      # The launcher scripts, staged out of the commit (stage-desktop-scripts.sh). tauri-build resolves the
      # resource glob while CARGO builds, so the three bare cargo steps below need it as much as a bundle does
      # — and the desktop-app `build` above, which stages on its own, is a turbo task that a cache hit skips.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/desktop/stage-desktop-scripts.sh
      - run: cargo fmt --manifest-path _editor/desktop-app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --manifest-path _editor/desktop-app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test --manifest-path _editor/desktop-app/src-tauri/Cargo.toml

  # The two shipped Rust crates that are not the desktop app: the ic host-side CLI (_sandbox/ic), the binary
  # behind the connect/recreate/connect-host bootstrap shims, and the Windows launcher stub
  # (_devices/win-launcher) the machine-side agents register at logon. Same cargo gate as the desktop crate —
  # fmt, clippy at -D warnings, tests — in the same image (it bakes the rust toolchain); no webkit/tauri in
  # either, so both are seconds off a warm registry.
  ic-check:
    needs: [changes, preflight, ci-base, ci-desktop]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.changes.outputs.ic == 'true' && needs.preflight.result == 'success' && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure' && needs.ci-desktop.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic, desktop]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      CARGO_HOME: /ci-cache/cargo
      # Its own target dir, for the same lock-and-fingerprint reasons desktop-check has its own.
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /ci-cache/ic-check-target
      # For the Windows half below (cargo-xwin) — the same shared MSVC splat every other cross-build uses.
      XWIN_CACHE_DIR: /ci-cache/xwin
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - run: cargo fmt --manifest-path _sandbox/ic/Cargo.toml --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --manifest-path _sandbox/ic/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
      # THE WINDOWS TARGET, because half of what this crate does for Windows is not compiled on Linux at all.
      # `prepare/` — the WSL2 + Docker Desktop setup, the largest single thing ic does on the platform it does
      # the most for — is one `#[cfg(windows)]` block, so the three steps above type-check straight past it. On
      # 2026-08-19 a `String` passed where a `&str` was wanted sat inside that block: fmt, clippy and the tests
      # were all green, the commit landed on main, and the FIRST thing that ever compiled the line was the
      # release's own cross-build — which failed, so the release did not happen. A gate that cannot see the code
      # is a gate the release is standing in for, and the release is the worst possible place to find out.
      #
      # `check`, not `clippy -D warnings`: this target carries warnings the Linux one does not (code that is
      # dead on Windows and live on unix, and vice versa), and silencing each with a cfg attribute would be a
      # steady tax for no defect caught. The compile error is what this is here for, and check catches it in
      # about the time clippy took.
      - run: cargo xwin check --manifest-path _sandbox/ic/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
      - run: cargo test --manifest-path _sandbox/ic/Cargo.toml
      # The launcher stub. The Windows target is not an extra here, it is the ONLY target the shipped binary is
      # ever built for: everything this crate does past argument parsing sits behind `#[cfg(windows)]`, so the
      # Linux fmt/clippy/test steps see the parser and nothing else. `clippy -D warnings` on the Linux side
      # (the crate is small enough to be clean there) and `xwin check` on the side that ships.
      - run: cargo fmt --manifest-path _devices/win-launcher/Cargo.toml --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --manifest-path _devices/win-launcher/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo xwin check --manifest-path _devices/win-launcher/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
      - run: cargo test --manifest-path _devices/win-launcher/Cargo.toml

  # The desktop ARTIFACTS: build the Linux bundles exactly the way the release builds them, then verify what
  # came out. Two tiers, ordered by cost, each proving something the one before it cannot:
  #
  #   1. build-desktop.sh ends by running verify-desktop-bundle.sh over its own output — the bundled scripts
  #      are present and byte-identical, and the .desktop entry registers intentic://. Seconds, no Docker.
  #   2. verify-desktop-install.sh installs the .deb and the AppImage on a BARE Debian (no GUI libraries),
  #      starts the app under Xvfb and fires a real xdg-open intentic:// at it. This is what catches an
  #      incomplete Depends field — a package that installs cleanly everywhere except a user's machine.
  #
  # NOT on pull requests: this is a release-profile Tauri build, and desktop-check's debug build + clippy +
  # tests is the fast gate. Tier 3 (verify-desktop-setup.sh, a real sandbox boot) is in nightly.yml.
  #
  # WINDOWS: the NSIS installer is also verified as an archive here (tier 1 reads it with 7z) — and EXECUTED by
  # the two jobs below, which is a thing no Linux runner can do.
  #
  # AND NOT WHEN THE RELEASE IS ABOUT TO DO IT PROPERLY. `release` builds this same tree at the REAL version —
  # linux-build runs the identical build-desktop.sh + verify-desktop-install.sh pair, windows-build +
  # windows-verify the identical Windows pair — and it does not need this job, so on a releasing push all of
  # this was a second set of artifacts, at 0.0.0, in their own cargo target directories (no cache shared with
  # the release's, by design), gating nothing. Four release-profile Tauri builds for one commit, and the two
  # Windows halves serialized on the ONE Windows machine, with the redundant one ahead of the release's in the
  # queue. The empty-version check is what keeps this job to the pushes where it is the only desktop coverage
  # there is; the release's own jobs are the coverage on every other one.
  desktop-verify:
    needs: [changes, preflight, ci-base, ci-desktop, release]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true' && needs.release.outputs.version == '' && needs.preflight.result == 'success' && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure' && needs.ci-desktop.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic, desktop]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      CARGO_HOME: /ci-cache/cargo
      # Its own directory, not the release's: this job always builds version 0.0.0 and the release always
      # builds a new one, so sharing meant each run invalidated the other's leaf crate and paid a fresh LTO
      # for it (~4 min). Apart is how this job rebuilds only when its OWN inputs changed.
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /ci-cache/desktop-verify-target
      INTENTIC_HOST_IMAGE: ghcr.io/intentic/dind-host:latest
      SANDBOX_E2E_IMAGE: ghcr.io/intentic/sandbox:latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/prepare-workspace
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      # A fixed 0.0.0: nothing here is published, and the version only names the bundle files.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/desktop/build-desktop.sh 0.0.0 --linux-only
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/desktop/verify-desktop-install.sh

  # What the Windows runner is handed. Built HERE, on Linux, because that is where the Windows installer has
  # always been built — cargo-xwin cross-compiles it, and this job is deliberately the same script the release
  # runs, so the bytes the Windows tier meets are produced by exactly the path that produces the released ones.
  #
  # Two artifacts, and the second is not optional. `connect.ps1` is a bootstrap SHIM: the setup flow lives in
  # the `ic` CLI, which the shim downloads from the LATEST GitHub Release. A Windows tier that let it do that
  # would be verifying the last release's flow against this commit's installer — so ic is cross-built from this
  # same checkout and handed to the shim through IC_BIN, its own local-dev override. The Linux setup tier does
  # exactly this, for exactly this reason.
  #
  # Gated on an empty release version for the reason desktop-verify spells out: on a releasing push the
  # release's own windows-build cross-builds this same installer at the real version and windows-verify runs
  # it on the same single Windows machine, so this pair was a redundant cross-build plus a redundant
  # install/uninstall cycle sitting AHEAD of the release's in that machine's queue.
  desktop-windows-build:
    needs: [changes, preflight, ci-base, ci-desktop, release]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && needs.changes.outputs.desktop == 'true' && needs.release.outputs.version == '' && needs.preflight.result == 'success' && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure' && needs.ci-desktop.result != 'failure' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic, desktop]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-desktop:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      CARGO_HOME: /ci-cache/cargo
      # Its own target dir, for the same lock-and-fingerprint reasons desktop-verify and ic-check have theirs.
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /ci-cache/desktop-windows-target
      # The MSVC CRT + Windows SDK cargo-xwin splats (~1.1 GB) — on the shared volume because its default lives
      # under $HOME/.cache, which dies with the container.
      XWIN_CACHE_DIR: /ci-cache/xwin
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/prepare-workspace
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/desktop/build-desktop.sh 0.0.0 --windows-only
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/build/build-ic.sh windows-x64
      # Staged into one directory rather than uploaded as two paths, because an upload of several paths is
      # rooted at their COMMON ANCESTOR — for two different dist-bin directories that is the repo root, and the
      # installer arrives under `_editor/desktop-app/dist-bin/` instead of at the top level the Windows tier
      # looks in. A directory upload is rooted at the directory, so the names survive.
      # No `rm -rf` first any more: this job checks out with `clean: false`, so the directory could survive a
      # run whose build failed after staging — which prepare-workspace above now removes as a matter of rule,
      # `windows-artifacts` being outside its allowlist, rather than as a line each staging step remembers.
      - run: |
          . _tools/scripts/lib/desktop-artifacts.sh
          mkdir -p windows-artifacts
          cp "$(desktop_artifact _editor/desktop-app/dist-bin nsis)" _sandbox/ic/dist-bin/ic-windows-amd64.exe windows-artifacts/
      - uses: ./.github/actions/upload-artifact-retry
        with:
          name: windows-desktop-artifacts
          path: windows-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  # THE TIER NO OTHER JOB IN THIS REPO CAN RUN: the shipped Windows installer, executed on Windows.
  #
  # Everything else this pipeline knows about the Windows installer comes from reading it as an archive. This
  # installs it unattended on a clean machine, asserts what landed on disk, fires a real intentic:// link at a
  # machine where the app has never run — the state a first-time user is in, and the half that was broken on
  # Linux for months while every after-launch assertion passed — launches it, fires the link again at the
  # running instance, and uninstalls it with the app still running (its tray is where it lives, so that is the
  # ordinary state at uninstall time).
  #
  # NO DOCKER, NO CREDENTIALS, NO NETWORK beyond the installer's own. That is what lets it gate main rather than
  # sit in the nightly: everything it asserts is a property of the package and the OS. The tiers that DO need a
  # Docker daemon and a connected account are in nightly.yml.
  #
  # `runs-on` names a label the Linux fleet does not carry, and that is load-bearing: `[self-hosted, intentic]`
  # is an AND over labels, so a Windows box carrying `intentic` would be handed container jobs it cannot run.
  # See docs/ci-runner-windows.md — including why this runner must be started from a logged-in session rather
  # than installed as a service (a service session has no desktop, and every assertion here reads a window).
  # Tier 1 only — everything it asserts is a property of the package and the OS, which is what lets it gate
  # main rather than sit in the nightly. The tiers that DO need a Docker daemon and a connected account are the
  # `deep` call in nightly.yml. A glob for the installer: this job builds at 0.0.0 and holds no version to
  # demand, unlike release.yml's call.
  desktop-verify-windows:
    needs: [desktop-windows-build]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.desktop-windows-build.result == 'success' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/windows-smoke.yml
    with:
      artifact-name: windows-desktop-artifacts
      installer: Intentic-*-x64-setup.exe

  # Hermetic infra e2e on pull requests — a NON-BLOCKING sidecar. Boots a Docker-in-Docker host via
  # testcontainers and drives the real CLI (resolve -> targeted apply -> adopt -> readiness diagnostics), no
  # external services and no secrets. Needing nothing at all is what earns it a run per pull request.
  e2e-hermetic:
    needs: preflight
    # The fork boundary again — see `changes`. Alone among the pull-request jobs this one's condition names no
    # `needs` output, so a skipped root does not reach it through the data; it has to say so itself.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    # allow_failure: true — it reports, it does not gate.
    continue-on-error: true
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      INTENTIC_HOST_IMAGE: ghcr.io/intentic/dind-host:latest
      INTENTIC_LOG_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.e2e-hermetic-logs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      - run: pnpm e2e:hermetic
      - uses: ./.github/actions/upload-artifact-retry
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: e2e-hermetic-logs
          path: .e2e-hermetic-logs/
          retention-days: 7

  # Continuous image publishing: build + push sandbox + dind-host on every push to main that touches the core
  # (moving `latest` + the commit SHA). The version-tagged image is the release job's.
  #
  # It needs `verify (core)` alone — not the whole matrix. A plain stage barrier would make this wait for the
  # SLOWEST group and skip outright if any of them failed, so a site build or a desktop clippy warning would
  # stop the images and the platform deploy for a reason neither has anything to do with. Both happened
  # before the edges were narrowed.
  #
  # AND NOT WHEN THE RELEASE BUILDS THE SAME IMAGE. On a releasing push the release's `images-amd64` and
  # `sandbox-arm64` build this same tree at the real version, and release-images.sh then moves `latest` onto
  # that build; this job and its arm64 twin were a second 46-minute build of the same bytes at 0.0.0, started a
  # minute apart on the same fleet, for a tag the release was about to move anyway. Same shape desktop-verify
  # uses: wait for the release call, run only when it released nothing. On a non-releasing push that wait is
  # the release's one-minute `plan`; a release that failed leaves `latest` to this job, as before.
  images:
    needs: [changes, verify-core, release]
    if: |
      !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      && needs.changes.outputs.images == 'true'
      && needs.verify-core.result == 'success'
      && (needs.release.outputs.version == '' || needs.release.result != 'success')
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    container:
      # ci-base (node + docker CLI), not a bare docker image: prepare-image-trees.sh compiles the payload
      # JOB-side — with the warm pnpm store + turbo cache from the verify matrix it is a cache replay — and the
      # Dockerfile is left with pure COPYs.
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # Publishes the sandbox and dind-host tags, so write here rather than in the workflow default.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    env:
      # Pinned rather than left to publish-images.sh's default: ghcr.io is the only registry the login below
      # authenticates to, and every extra entry costs a second ~1.5 GB upload plus two more `--cache-from`
      # probes per image. Adding a registry here means adding a login step for it too.
      REGISTRIES: ghcr.io/intentic
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # The iq models (~57 MB, fetched from HuggingFace) that prepare-image-trees.sh bakes into the sandbox
      # image's `trees` context. That script skips the download when .iq-models-complete is already there, so
      # this cache is the whole reason the fetch happens once per change of fetch-model.mjs rather than once
      # per pipeline. It stays an Actions cache rather than moving to /ci-cache for one reason: the directory
      # has to land inside .image-out, and this job and `release` run CONCURRENTLY — one shared directory
      # would need the fetch to be race-safe first.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            .image-out/iq-models
            .image-out/.iq-models-complete
          key: iq-models-${{ hashFiles('_search/iq-engine/scripts/fetch-model.mjs') }}

      - run: bash _tools/scripts/image/prepare-image-trees.sh
      # `shell: bash` because the job's default is `sh`, where the `${VAR::N}` slice below is a Bad substitution.
      # The sandbox pushes per-arch tags (this runner is the amd64 half; images-arm64 is the other) and the
      # merge job publishes the plain multi-arch tags; dind-host stays single-arch (publish-images.sh says why).
      - run: TAGS="latest sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}" ARCH_SUFFIX=-amd64 IMAGES=sandbox bash _tools/scripts/image/publish-images.sh
        shell: bash
      # THE HALVES MUST BOOT BEFORE ANY MOVING TAG POINTS AT THEM. Everything upstream of this job ran in the
      # development install; the image runs a `pnpm deploy --prod` tree, and a daemon that dies on an import
      # missing from THAT tree leaves every check above green (smoke-image.sh's header tells the story). This
      # is the first and only per-push step that starts the artifact. It runs against the SHA tags just pushed
      # — the published bytes, not a local build — and a red step means images-merge never stitches `latest`,
      # so consumers stay on the previous good pair.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/image/smoke-image.sh "ghcr.io/intentic/sandbox:sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}-amd64" "ghcr.io/intentic/sandbox:core-sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}-amd64"
        shell: bash
      # NO `latest` HERE, deliberately — the immutable SHA tag only. dind-host has no halves to stitch, so it
      # used to get its moving tag written right here, in the same step that built it, while sandbox:latest
      # waited for images-merge. That made the two images move at different times, and images-arm64 is the leg
      # most likely to fail: when it did, the registry held a NEW dind-host:latest beside the PREVIOUS
      # sandbox:latest — a pair nothing had tested together, and the pair nightly's tiers, verify-images-public
      # and the shipped connect-host.ps1 all reference by name. images-merge promotes this tag once both
      # sandbox halves are in, so the two images move together or neither does.
      - run: TAGS="sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}" IMAGES=dind-host bash _tools/scripts/image/publish-images.sh
        shell: bash

  # The sandbox image's arm64 half, natively built — GitHub's hosted arm runners rather than the x86 fleet,
  # because the trees payload must be prepared on the arch it ships for (pnpm deploy fetches the HOST arch's
  # native prebuilds; publish-images.sh says the rest). Cold caches by construction (no /ci-cache off the
  # fleet): pnpm's store rides setup-node's cache, turbo rebuilds, and the docker build warms itself off the
  # registry's own arm64 tags. The release does NOT reuse these sha tags — its arm64 half is version-stamped
  # inside release.yml (sandbox-arm64 there) so a released manifest's halves never skew.
  images-arm64:
    needs: [changes, verify-core, release]
    # Gated on the release the way `images` is: the release's sandbox-arm64 builds this half on a releasing push.
    if: |
      !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      && needs.changes.outputs.images == 'true'
      && needs.verify-core.result == 'success'
      && (needs.release.outputs.version == '' || needs.release.result != 'success')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    # OFF THE FLEET, SO OFF THE FLEET'S CACHE. The workflow-level TURBO_CACHE_DIR names /ci-cache, a host
    # directory the self-hosted runners mount and a GitHub-hosted one has never heard of. The header above says
    # an absent mount falls back "cold, never broken" — true of pnpm, not of turbo, which CREATES the directory
    # it is pointed at and dies on the permission error, /ci-cache being at the filesystem root. Overridden per
    # job rather than dropped from the workflow env, because every other job here does want the shared one.
    # PNPM_STORE needs no override: only the pnpm-setup composite reads it, and this job does not use it.
    env:
      TURBO_CACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.turbo-cache
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@fc06bc1257f339d1d5d8b3a19a8cae5388b55320 # v4.4.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6.5.0
        with:
          node-version-file: package.json
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            .image-out/iq-models
            .image-out/.iq-models-complete
          key: iq-models-${{ hashFiles('_search/iq-engine/scripts/fetch-model.mjs') }}
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/image/prepare-image-trees.sh
      - run: TAGS="latest sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}" ARCH_SUFFIX=-arm64 IMAGES=sandbox bash _tools/scripts/image/publish-images.sh
        shell: bash
      # The arm64 half's own boot gate — the counterpart of the amd64 one above, and the reason it runs HERE
      # rather than once somewhere central: an image can only be booted on the architecture it was built for,
      # so each half is proven on the runner that produced it. SMOKE_RMI because this is a GitHub-hosted runner
      # with a hosted runner's disk (smoke-image.sh says why the pull is a second copy).
      - run: SMOKE_RMI=1 bash _tools/scripts/image/smoke-image.sh "ghcr.io/intentic/sandbox:sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}-arm64" "ghcr.io/intentic/sandbox:core-sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}-arm64"
        shell: bash

  # Stitch the two halves into the plain tags — two manifest calls per tag, no bytes moved. Until this runs,
  # `latest` still points at the previous merge, so a consumer mid-pipeline never sees a half-published tag.
  #
  # THE MOVING TAGS OF BOTH IMAGES ARE WRITTEN HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. dind-host has no halves to stitch, so its
  # `latest` used to be written by the `images` job directly — which meant the pair could skew whenever the
  # arm64 half failed. Its promotion is a one-source manifest copy, gated by the same `needs` as the sandbox
  # stitch, so the two images now move together or neither moves.
  images-merge:
    needs: [images, images-arm64]
    if: ${{ needs.images.result == 'success' && needs.images-arm64.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    env:
      REGISTRIES: ghcr.io/intentic
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/image/merge-image-manifests.sh sandbox latest "sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}" core-latest "core-sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}"
        shell: bash
      # The single-arch half of the same promise: point dind-host's `latest` at the SHA tag the `images` job
      # pushed. Last, so a failed sandbox stitch leaves both images on the previous pair rather than one of each.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/image/promote-image-tag.sh dind-host "sha-${GITHUB_SHA::8}" latest
        shell: bash

  # Platform image publishing: build + push web + api on every push to main that touches the platform, then
  # roll the Komodo stack. Same philosophy as `images` — apps build job-side under turbo off the warm caches,
  # and the Dockerfiles are pure COPY. docker:release's TURBO_HASH tag makes the release content-addressed, so
  # the path filter is deliberately COARSE: a push that didn't change an app's actual inputs just re-tags the
  # existing image registry-side.
  images-platform:
    needs: [changes, verify-platform]
    if: |
      !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      && needs.changes.outputs.platform == 'true'
      && needs.verify-platform.result == 'success'
    runs-on: [self-hosted, intentic]
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/intentic/ci-base:latest
      volumes:
        - /ci-cache:/ci-cache
        - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      credentials:
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # Publishes the platform images — same reason as `images`.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    env:
      # Same pin as the `images` job — docker-release.sh carries the identical default, and this job
      # authenticates to ghcr.io only.
      REGISTRIES: ghcr.io/intentic
      PLATFORM_DEPLOY_STACK: intentic-platform
      KOMODO_URL: ${{ secrets.KOMODO_URL }}
      KOMODO_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.KOMODO_API_KEY }}
      KOMODO_API_SECRET: ${{ secrets.KOMODO_API_SECRET }}
      # WHERE THE SMOKE TEST'S BROWSER LANDS, and the answer must not be $HOME. `playwright install` defaults to
      # `$HOME/.cache/ms-playwright`, which in a job container is `/github/home` — a directory the runner process
      # KEEPS BETWEEN JOBS. So this job left a Chromium sitting where every later job on that runner would find
      # it, and ci-base ships none of Chromium's shared libraries. The sandbox's browser suites stand down when
      # `chromium.executablePath()` does not exist; here it existed, so they launched it and died on
      # `libglib-2.0.so.0: cannot open shared object file`. Two suites that are correct in git failed an hour
      # after this job ran, in a pipeline that never asked for a browser.
      # The shared cache instead: warm across runs (this download is ~200 MB), and invisible to every job that
      # does not name this variable. pnpm-setup clears the strays the old default already wrote.
      PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: /ci-cache/ms-playwright
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          clean: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/pnpm-setup
      - uses: ./.github/actions/ghcr-login
        with:
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - run: pnpm turbo run docker:release --filter=@intentic/api --filter=@intentic/web --filter=@intentic/ingress
      # `shell: bash` because the job's default is `sh`, where the `${VAR::N}` slice below is a Bad substitution.
      - run: DEPLOY_VERSION="${GITHUB_SHA::8}" bash _tools/scripts/platform/deploy-platform.sh
        shell: bash

      # AND THE EDGE, which the step above does not roll and for ten days nobody noticed it didn't. The Komodo
      # stack is the api and the web; the ingress runs on Fly, so pushing its image above changed nothing about
      # what production was serving. Hosted sandboxes had meanwhile moved onto `fly-replay`, which the running
      # edge was too old to do, so each one answered 502 at its own address and told its owner to start it over.
      # deploy-ingress.sh rolls it and then reads the build back off the public /health, so a push that does not
      # land is a red job rather than a silent one.
      #
      # Inert without FLY_API_TOKEN, exactly as deploy-platform.sh is without a stack: a fork sees a skip.
      - run: bash _tools/scripts/platform/deploy-ingress.sh
        shell: bash
        env:
          FLY_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLY_API_TOKEN }}

      # AND THEN CHECK THAT A STRANGER CAN STILL SIGN IN, which nothing else here does.
      #
      # The step above proves the api boots and answers /health. It says nothing about the front door, and the
      # front door is not ours alone: sign-in also depends on Google still accepting this origin for the OAuth
      # client, which is state living in a console outside this repo and outside this pipeline. When that
      # stopped being true, every Google button on the site went dead and the whole pipeline stayed green —
      # the browser tier runs on a seeded session with no real Google, and so does every unit test.
      #
      # It is a real browser because it has to be: the same request answers 200 to curl and 400 to Chromium
      # (smoke-signin.mjs has the evidence), so an HTTP probe would have been green throughout the outage.
      # That is the whole cost justification for installing a browser in a deploy job.
      - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
        working-directory: _tools/e2e
      - run: pnpm smoke:signin "${WEB_ORIGIN}"
        working-directory: _tools/e2e
        env:
          WEB_ORIGIN: https://app.intentic.dev

  # The whole release lifecycle is one reusable-workflow call because the exact NSIS candidate has to cross an
  # OS boundary before semantic-release may publish. The call holds the `release` concurrency lock throughout:
  # plan version → cross-build once → execute on Windows → stage those same bytes → publish. A lock on only the
  # final Linux job would let two pipelines plan the same next version while the first candidate was on Windows.
  # verify-providers is a REQUIRED success, spelled the same way verify-core is rather than the permissive
  # `!= 'failure'` the two image jobs get. Those two are allowed to be skipped; this one is not, because the
  # whole point of it is that a release cannot be cut without every provider's real CLI having been driven. A
  # gate that a skip satisfies is a gate that disappears exactly when someone disables it.
  release:
    needs: [verify-core, verify-providers, ci-base, ci-desktop]
    if: |
      !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      && needs.verify-core.result == 'success'
      && needs.verify-providers.result == 'success'
      && needs.ci-base.result != 'failure'
      && needs.ci-desktop.result != 'failure'
    concurrency:
      group: release
      cancel-in-progress: false
    uses: ./.github/workflows/release.yml
    secrets: inherit
    # A called workflow can never hold more than the caller grants, so this set is the CEILING for every job in
    # release.yml — a permission the publish job names and this list omits fails the whole pipeline before a
    # single job starts, as an invalid-workflow error that names neither.
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      # publish dispatches npm-publish.yml once the tag exists.
      actions: write
