build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "kindly-web-search-mcp-server"
version = "0.1.9"
description = "MCP server: Serper web search + robust content retrieval."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
# Every bound below comes from §10.2 of `.system_design/TEST_SUITE.md` and is
# asserted against it, in both directions, by `tests/test_dependency_constraints.py`.
#
# These are the bounds that reach users. The documented install path
# (`uvx --from git+https://...`) re-resolves every one of them from PyPI on each
# start and ignores any lock file, so a breaking major arrives with no commit here,
# no CI run and no alert — the first signal is a user whose server stops starting.
# Nine of these ten were bare names while the identical rule was already enforced
# for the tooling extras below: the dependencies developers install were guarded
# and the dependencies users install were not.
#
# Each ceiling is the next major of the version the entry was verified against, and
# each floor is that version's minor series — for nine of the ten. `mcp`'s floor is
# the older `>=1.25`, the oldest release verified against this server, which the
# guard pins separately; applying the nine-package rule to it would raise it to
# `>=1.29` and fail `test_mcp_requirement_still_allows_supported_version`. Same
# purpose, different number, and the difference is deliberate.
# "Verified" means a clean resolve into a fresh CPython 3.13 environment on
# 2026-09-06, after which the server module, `CORSMiddleware` and `FastMCP` were all
# imported successfully — on CPython 3.13 **and** 3.14, both of which this project
# supports and neither of which any wired CI leg resolves on. Same ten versions on
# both, compiled wheels included. Raising a bound is a deliberate PR that runs the full suite
# against the new version; Dependabot may propose, never auto-merge.
dependencies = [
    # `<2`: the MCP SDK dropped `mcp.server.fastmcp` in 2.0.0, and `server.py` imports
    # `FastMCP` from it. The documented install path (`uvx --from git+https://...`)
    # re-resolves from PyPI on every start and ignores `uv.lock`, so leaving this
    # unbounded broke every user the moment 2.0.0 shipped. Lift this bound only
    # alongside a port to the 2.x `MCPServer` API.
    # `>=1.25`: oldest release verified against this server; stops a constrained
    # resolve from silently selecting an older, untested API.
    "mcp>=1.25,<2",
    # `server.py` imports both directly to wrap the ASGI app in CORS middleware and
    # serve it. They arrive transitively via `mcp` today, which is exactly the kind of
    # undeclared dependency `tests/test_dependency_constraints.py` exists to catch.
    #
    # `starlette<2` and not `<1`: 1.0 shipped 22 March 2026 and is the current line —
    # a clean resolve selects 1.6.0, and this project crossed that major without
    # noticing while the entry was unbounded. The 1.0 break was the removal of
    # `on_startup`/`on_shutdown` in favour of `lifespan`, and this server uses
    # neither: it only wraps the ASGI app `FastMCP` builds. 1.0 did also change
    # `CORSMiddleware` itself — it now returns an explicit origin when credentials
    # are allowed, rather than a wildcard — which is the one 1.0 change that touches
    # the single starlette symbol `server.py` imports. The suite is green on 1.6.0,
    # so it is compatible in practice; it is named here because a justification that
    # only mentioned the change NOT affecting us would be the weaker half of the
    # truth. Bounding below 1.0 would roll users back off the release they already
    # run, to avoid a break that does not apply to this code.
    "starlette>=1.6,<2",
    # 🔴 `uvicorn`, `nodriver`, `httpx` and `PyMuPDF` have ceilings that are NOMINAL:
    # the first two are pre-1.0 where a minor may break, `PyMuPDF` removes API in 1.x
    # minors, and `httpx` is unlikely ever to ship 1.0 — its maintained successor is a
    # differently named distribution, `httpx2`. Do not read `<1` or `<2` on these four
    # as protection. Kept anyway because they still block a surprise major at no cost,
    # and because pinning each to one minor would force a PR per upstream minor on a
    # path that re-resolves at every user launch. §10.2 records the full reasoning and
    # what protects them instead.
    "uvicorn>=0.52,<1",
    # `mcp` requires `pydantic>=2.11,<3`; this floor is the verified release, which is
    # inside that range, so the two constraints resolve together rather than fighting.
    "pydantic>=2.13,<3",
    # The `[socks]` extra is load-bearing: it installs `socksio`, without which a
    # SOCKS proxy configuration fails at request time rather than at install time.
    "httpx[socks]>=0.28,<1",
    # `beautifulsoup4` and `markdownify` are the fallback extraction path in
    # `scrape/extract.py`, used when `trafilatura` returns nothing; `markdownify`
    # also serves the StackExchange loader. Both are imported behind try/except,
    # so a breaking major degrades content quality silently rather than failing at
    # import -- which is why a ceiling matters more here, not less.
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.15,<5",
    "markdownify>=1.2,<2",
    # Primary main-content extraction: a breaking major here is the difference
    # between a page and an empty string, and `scrape/extract.py` imports it behind
    # try/except, so the failure would arrive as blank content, not a crash.
    "trafilatura>=2.2,<3",
    # The headless Chromium worker behind the universal HTML loader. Pre-1.0 and
    # fast-moving; `<1` is the nominal ceiling described in the block above, and
    # `scrape/nodriver_worker.py` is the only consumer.
    "nodriver>=0.50,<1",
    # PDF to text for the arXiv loader. `<2` is nominal -- PyMuPDF has been 1.x
    # throughout and removes API in minors -- see the block above and §10.2.
    "PyMuPDF>=1.28,<2",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Every bound below comes from §10.2 of `.system_design/TEST_SUITE.md` and is
# asserted by `tests/test_dependency_constraints.py`. They are bounds rather than
# "current" because this project has twice been broken by an unbounded dependency.
# Raising one is a deliberate PR that runs the full suite against the new version;
# Dependabot may propose, never auto-merge.
#
# `packaging` is declared rather than inherited from pytest: the dependency-bound
# guard in `tests/test_dependency_constraints.py` imports it directly, and relying
# on a transitive dep is the same failure mode that guard exists to prevent.
dev = [
    "pytest>=9,<10",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2",
    "hypothesis>=6.167,<7",
    "coverage>=7.10.3,<8",
    "diff-cover>=10.4,<11",
    "ruff>=0.6,<1",
    "mypy>=2.3.1,<3",
    "packaging>=24",
]
# `mutmut` needs `fork()` and therefore only runs on Linux/WSL. It is kept out of
# `dev` so the extra everyone installs stays installable everywhere.
#
# This extra is ADDITIVE, never installed alone: `mutmut` drives pytest over the
# L1 suite, which needs `hypothesis` and `pytest-asyncio`, and mutmut declares
# neither. The nightly mutation job installs `.[dev,mutation]`. Installing this
# extra by itself yields a mutmut whose test command fails at import — which
# reads as "tests fail on unmutated code", not as a missing dependency.
mutation = ["mutmut>=3,<4"]
# The pinned environment §10.4's coverage baseline is measured in.
# `requirements-ratchet.txt` is the frozen transitive closure of this extra and is
# what that lane is designed to install — no workflow installs it yet, and `ci.yml`
# says so; this list is the input that regenerates it.
#
# `coverage` is pinned exactly rather than range-bounded because a patch release
# that moved a two-decimal total would fail the ratchet for reasons unrelated to
# the change under test. `ruff` is absent because linting is not measurement, and
# `mutmut` because it is Linux-only and belongs to the nightly. `packaging` is
# present for the same reason it is in `dev`: the guard module imports it
# directly. It does resolve transitively through `pytest`, so declaring it changes
# nothing about whether the lane runs — only whether the declaration is honest,
# which is the whole point of that guard.
ratchet = [
    "pytest>=9,<10",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2",
    "hypothesis>=6.167,<7",
    "coverage==7.13.5",
    "diff-cover>=10.4,<11",
    "packaging>=24",
]
# Optional extras for improved PDF-to-Markdown conversion on supported Python versions.
# These pull in `onnxruntime` transitively (via `pymupdf-layout`), which may not have wheels
# for the newest CPython releases (e.g., cp314). Keeping them optional avoids install
# failures while preserving a simple text-extraction baseline via PyMuPDF.
pdf-advanced = [
    "pymupdf-layout>=1.26.6; python_version < '3.14'",
    "pymupdf4llm>=0.2.7; python_version < '3.14'",
]

[project.scripts]

mcp-web-search = "kindly_web_search_mcp_server.server:main"
kindly-web-search = "kindly_web_search_mcp_server.server:main"
kindly-web-search-mcp-server = "kindly_web_search_mcp_server.cli:main"

# Section 10.5 of `.system_design/TEST_SUITE.md`. That section is the policy and
# this table is what the runner reads; `tests/test_pytest_configuration.py`
# asserts they agree in both directions, so a docs-only edit there turns the
# suite red. Change both in the same PR.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
# Forward-looking: nothing outside `tests/` is collected today either, because
# pytest's default `norecursedirs` already skips `.github/`. It matters once
# E3-5 adds `tests/package/`, which §10.3's jobs select and deselect explicitly.
testpaths = ["tests"]
# The ini option, NOT `addopts = "--strict-markers"` as earlier drafts of §10.5
# had it. pytest 9.0.0 through 9.0.3 silently ignore strictness flags that arrive
# through `addopts` (pytest#14442, fixed in 9.1.0), and `pytest>=9,<10` allows
# them. Measured across 9.0.0-9.1.1: on every 9.0.x the `addopts` form leaves an
# unregistered marker passing at exit 0; this form aborts collection at exit 2 on
# all of them. A marker that is
# accepted but unregistered is the worst case available here -- the test it
# labels is excluded from every marker-selected job while still reporting green.
strict_markers = true
# Makes an unknown or misspelled ini option a hard error rather than a warning
# nobody reads. Concretely: without it, an environment missing `pytest-asyncio`
# degrades `asyncio_mode` to a `PytestConfigWarning` and then fails every async
# test with "async def functions are not natively supported" -- a symptom three
# steps removed from the cause. With it, the run stops at
# `ERROR: Unknown config option: asyncio_mode`.
strict_config = true
# §10.1: the project is pure asyncio, so the `asyncio` marker is noise. The
# existing `unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase` classes are unaffected --
# pytest-asyncio does not handle unittest classes at all -- so this changes no
# result today and is what E11's migration lands onto.
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Set explicitly because leaving it unset is not neutral: pytest-asyncio 1.4
# raises a `PytestDeprecationWarning` during `pytest_configure` -- before the
# warnings plugin can capture it, so it never reaches the warnings summary --
# announcing that a future release will flip the async-fixture loop default from
# "fixture" caching scope to "function". `pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2` allows that
# release, and it would land on E11, the step that converts the whole suite.
# "function" is the announced future default, chosen so the flip is a no-op.
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
# All seven of §10.5. `slow` now has a real user --
# `tests/test_baseline_failure_ledger.py`, which spawns a child run of the whole
# suite -- alongside the control case in `tests/test_pytest_configuration.py`.
markers = [
    "live: hits the real network; needs KINDLY_RUN_LIVE_TESTS=1",
    "subsystem: needs a real socket or child process; portable",
    "chromium: needs a real browser; Linux container only",
    "package: runs against an installed wheel, not the source tree",
    "serper: live test requiring SERPER_API_KEY",
    "extraction: live content-extraction canary; browser, no credential",
    "slow: over a second",
]

# The first mypy configuration in this repository, added with the worker-process
# Protocol. Section 10.3 of `.system_design/TEST_SUITE.md` is the policy: the
# type-check job is deliberately narrow. It runs over the modules that declare or
# implement the test-double Protocols, not the whole tree -- repo-wide type
# checking on ~6,849 largely unannotated lines is its own project. This job
# exists for one purpose, catching the signature drift that `runtime_checkable`
# cannot see, and is scoped to earn its place immediately.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
# `files` makes the narrow target reproducible: a bare `mypy` from the repository
# root checks exactly the surface the job is scoped to, so the harness and a
# developer's local run cannot diverge.
files = [
    "src/kindly_web_search_mcp_server/scrape/types.py",
    # The seam itself. Production annotates the process it spawns with
    # `WorkerProcess`, so this is what makes mypy compare the Protocol against
    # what production actually reads -- the direction an introspection test
    # cannot reach, because it sees only the Protocol.
    "src/kindly_web_search_mcp_server/scrape/worker_runner.py",
    "tests/doubles",
]
# There is no `py.typed` marker under `src/`, and the project is installed as a
# modern editable. Without this, mypy reports `Skipping analyzing
# "kindly_web_search_mcp_server.scrape": module is installed, but missing library
# stubs or py.typed marker [import-untyped]`, `WorkerProcess` degrades to `Any`,
# and EVERY conformance assignment passes vacuously -- the positive harness case
# goes green on a completely broken configuration. Adding `py.typed` is the
# alternative and is deliberately not taken: it publishes this project's types to
# downstream consumers, a wider commitment than a test harness should make.
#
# `$MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR` is required, not cosmetic. A relative `mypy_path`
# resolves against the mypy process's working directory, not this file's
# location, so a child invocation started elsewhere would silently lose the path.
# The harness pins `cwd` to the repository root as well; either alone is a
# single point of failure.
mypy_path = "$MYPY_CONFIG_FILE_DIR/src"
# Catches a per-module section below whose `module` key matches nothing -- the
# silent failure this configuration is most exposed to, because a mistyped key
# disables its settings with no warning and a test that merely reads the setting
# out of this file still passes.
#
# mypy's documentation says reporting this "requires turning off incremental
# mode". Measured on the pinned 2.3.1, it reports either way, cold cache and
# warm, so `incremental = false` is NOT set: it cost 1.74s against 0.15s per
# invocation, and the harness makes seven of them. Because that leaves the guard
# resting on undocumented behaviour, `test_unused_configuration_sections_are_reported`
# proves the reporting still happens rather than assuming it -- if a future mypy
# starts honouring its own documentation, that case goes red instead of this
# guard going quiet.
warn_unused_configs = true
# A file that MUST fail type-checking cannot sit in the path the job checks, or
# the job is red forever. Note that `exclude` removes a file from DISCOVERY only:
# it is ignored for a file named explicitly on the command line, which is how the
# harness reaches these fixtures, and it does not remove them from CONFIGURATION.
#
# Do NOT add a per-module override for them here. It would match nothing on an
# ordinary run, `warn_unused_configs` would report it, and
# `test_ordinary_target_reports_no_unused_configuration_sections` would go red.
# The one fixture needing non-default strictness declares it inline with a
# `# mypy:` comment instead; the other three fail under mypy's own defaults and
# need no configuration at all.
exclude = ["(^|/)tests/typing_negative/"]

# The Protocol and the double built against it. `disallow_any_expr` is what
# catches an `Any` arriving by INFERENCE inside these modules -- neither
# `disallow_any_explicit` (written-out `Any` annotations only) nor
# `disallow_untyped_defs` (unannotated definitions only) sees that case.
#
# It is NOT what rejects a mock substituted for the double: `AsyncMock()` has
# type `AsyncMock`, not `Any`, so no expression here is ever flagged. The
# `assert_type` block in `tests/doubles/worker_process.py` is that mechanism.
# Both are needed; neither is redundant.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "kindly_web_search_mcp_server.scrape.types",
    "tests.doubles.worker_process",
]
disallow_any_expr = true

repository.description: Multi-tenant memory and reasoning substrate for AI agents, with eleven business engines on top. Python, Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, MinIO. MCP + REST.
repository.name: neuro-cognitive-engine
repository.readme:
# NCE — Neuro-Cognitive Engine > A cognitive memory and reasoning substrate for autonomous agents. > Persistent, multi-tenant, time-travelling memory across a four-database stack — with a brain on top.

NCE began life as **TriMCP** — a Model Context Protocol server backed by a tri-database stack. It has since grown into a full **Neuro-Cognitive Engine**: MCP is now just *one* of several front doors onto a system that consolidates memories while agents sleep, models how knowledge decays and is reinforced, maintains logical consistency across competing beliefs, reasons about cause and effect, and federates memory securely between independent agent networks. The engine is **provider-agnostic** (BYO LLM — local, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and more), **multi-tenant by construction** (database-enforced Row-Level Security), and **auditable by design** (an append-only, hash-chained event log that makes every state reconstructable and every memory's causal provenance traceable). --- ## Table of Contents - [Why NCE](#why-nce) - [The Cognitive Model](#the-cognitive-model) - [System Architecture](#system-architecture) - [The Quad-Database Stack](#the-quad-database-stack) - [Capabilities](#capabilities) - [Surfaces & Entrypoints](#surfaces--entrypoints) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [Connecting an MCP Client](#connecting-an-mcp-client) - [MCP Tool Surface](#mcp-tool-surface) - [Security Model](#security-model) - [Vertical Modules](#vertical-modules) - [Tech Stack](#tech-stack) - [Testing & Quality Gates](#testing--quality-gates) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Production Checklist](#production-checklist) --- ## Why NCE Most "agent memory" is a vector index with a `search()` call bolted on. That works until an agent runs for weeks, serves multiple tenants, accumulates contradictory facts, and someone asks *"what did the agent believe last Tuesday, and why?"* NCE is built for that second world: | Concern | Naïve approach | NCE | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Recall** | Flat vector search | Semantic search **+** GraphRAG traversal **+** spiking spreading activation | | **Isolation** | App-layer `WHERE tenant = ?` | PostgreSQL **Row-Level Security**, forced on every table | | **History** | Last-write-wins | Append-only **WORM event log**; `as_of` time-travel on every read | | **Knowledge quality** | Store everything forever | **Consolidation** (sleep cycle), **salience decay**, **contradiction detection** | | **Truth** | Trust the latest write | **ATMS** belief revision with justification graphs | | **Sharing** | Copy data between agents | **A2A** cryptographic, scope-bound, RLS-enforced federation | | **Auditability** | Logs, maybe | Hash-chained provenance; deterministic **replay & fork** of any namespace | --- ## The Cognitive Model NCE treats memory the way a mind does — as a lifecycle, not a bucket. ``` ingest ──▶ EPISODIC ──▶ consolidate ──▶ SEMANTIC ──▶ knowledge graph (raw) memories (sleep cycle) abstractions (entities + relations) │ │ salience decay spreading activation (Ebbinghaus curve) (neuromorphic recall) │ │ reinforced ◀──────────── retrieval ───────────────────┘ ``` - **Episodic → Semantic consolidation.** A background "sleep cycle" runs HDBSCAN density clustering over episodic embeddings, distils each cluster into a *Semantic Abstraction* via an LLM (output strictly validated by Pydantic V2), and upserts the result into both the memory store and the knowledge graph. - **Salience & forgetting.** Every memory carries a salience score that decays exponentially per the **Ebbinghaus forgetting curve**, `s(t) = s₀·e^(−λΔt)`, and is reinforced on retrieval, `s ← min(1.0, s + δ)`. Important things stay sharp; noise fades. - **Contradiction detection.** New facts are checked against existing knowledge via semantic match → KG conflict → a **cross-encoder NLI** model (`nli-deberta-v3-small`) → an LLM tiebreaker. Unresolved conflicts are surfaced for the agent to settle. - **Belief revision (ATMS).** An Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance System tracks `ASSUMPTION` / `PREMISE` / `DERIVED` nodes and their justifications, propagating deprecation through the justification graph (cycle-safe) when an assumption is retracted. - **Causal reasoning.** A do-calculus causal engine and counterfactual **chrono-branching** let agents ask *"what if"* — overlaying hypothetical mutations on an isolated timeline without ever touching production rows. See [docs/cognitive_layer.md](docs/cognitive_layer.md) and [docs/netbox_and_cognitive_extensions.md](docs/netbox_and_cognitive_extensions.md). --- ## System Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Clients [Clients] IDE[MCP clients · Claude Desktop · Cursor] PEER[Peer agent networks] OPS[Operators / Admins] end subgraph Surfaces [Surfaces] STDIO[server.py · MCP stdio] A2A[a2a_server.py · A2A federation] ADM[admin_server.py · REST + Admin UI] WH[webhook_receiver · document bridges] end subgraph Background [Background processing] RQ[start_worker.py · RQ worker] CRON[nce.cron · schedulers] end subgraph Engine [NCEEngine — orchestration] ORCH[Saga write path] COG[Cognitive workers] TMP[Temporal / replay] end subgraph Data [Quad-Database Stack] PG[(PostgreSQL + pgvector)] MG[(MongoDB)] RD[(Redis)] S3[(MinIO)] end IDE --> STDIO PEER --> A2A OPS --> ADM STDIO --> ORCH A2A --> ORCH ADM --> ORCH WH --> RQ RQ --> ORCH CRON --> COG ORCH --> PG & MG & RD & S3 COG --> PG & MG TMP --> PG & S3 ``` Every standard write travels a transaction-scoped **Saga** path with automatic compensating rollbacks, so a partial failure across the four stores never leaves orphaned state. Detailed sequence diagrams live in [docs/architecture-v1.md](docs/architecture-v1.md) and [docs/database_architecture.md](docs/database_architecture.md). --- ## The Quad-Database Stack Duties are split across four engines so each does only what it is best at: | Store | Role | Holds | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **PostgreSQL + pgvector** | Relational core & vector index | Semantic embeddings (HNSW), knowledge-graph triplets (`kg_nodes` / `kg_edges`), RLS policies, the WORM `event_log` | | **MongoDB** | Episodic payload archive | Heavy unstructured content — transcripts, code, document pages — referenced by ObjectID | | **Redis** | Transient & coordination | TTL context caches, rate limits, distributed locks, single-use HMAC nonces, RQ job queues | | **MinIO** | Object storage (S3 API) | Binary artifacts (image/audio/video) and the deterministic LLM response cache used by replay | --- ## Capabilities - **Hybrid recall** — `semantic_search` (pgvector cosine) with MongoDB hydration, `graph_search` GraphRAG BFS traversal, and neuromorphic **spiking spreading activation** with LTP/LTD weight adaptation. - **Time travel** — pass an `as_of` ISO-8601 timestamp to any read and see memory exactly as it stood: `valid_from <= as_of AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > as_of)`. Applies symmetrically to vector search and graph traversal. - **Snapshots & state diffing** — name a point in time (`create_snapshot`) and diff two instants with `compare_states`. - **Replay engine** — `replay_observe` streams the event log read-only; `replay_fork` rebuilds a namespace into an isolated target, either *deterministically* (LLM responses served from the MinIO cache, byte-identical) or *re-executed* (call the LLM fresh for A/B "what-if" divergence); `replay_reconstruct` for exact rebuilds. - **Code intelligence** — `index_code_file` AST-parses source (Tree-sitter; Python, JS, TS, Go, Rust) into per-symbol chunks; `search_codebase` returns matching functions/classes with line ranges. - **Document bridges** — OAuth + webhook sync from **SharePoint/OneDrive, Google Drive, and Dropbox**, with subscription renewal, retry, and a dead-letter queue. - **Rich ingestion** — extractors for PDF, Office (Word/Excel/PowerPoint), email, CAD, diagrams, project files, plaintext, with OCR and LibreOffice fallbacks. - **Provider-agnostic cognition** — `local-cognitive-model`, `openai`, `azure_openai`, `anthropic`, `google_gemini`, `deepseek`, `moonshot_kimi`, and any `openai_compatible` endpoint. - **Edge & air-gapped** — local inference stack with optional **OpenVINO NPU** acceleration; see [docs/airgapped_deployment.md](docs/airgapped_deployment.md). - **Observability** — OpenTelemetry → OTLP/Jaeger tracing and a Prometheus metrics endpoint, on by default. --- ## Surfaces & Entrypoints NCE is no longer "just an MCP server." It exposes several coordinated surfaces: | Entrypoint | Transport | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `server.py` | MCP stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0) | Tool surface for LLM clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) | | `admin_server.py` | HTTP (Starlette REST + Admin UI) | Operations, namespace/quota management, runtime tool toggles | | `nce/a2a_server.py` | HTTP (A2A RPC) | Federated, scope-bound memory sharing between agent networks | | `nce/webhook_receiver` | HTTP | Inbound document-bridge change notifications | | `start_worker.py` | RQ worker | Async jobs — code indexing, bridge sync, re-embedding | | `nce/cron.py` | Scheduler | Consolidation cycles, bridge renewal, GC | A **Dynamic Tools Console** in the Admin UI can enable/disable individual stdio tools or A2A skills at runtime (persisted to a Redis hash); disabled calls are rejected by the dispatch interceptor. If Redis is unreachable the interceptor fails *open* to avoid cascading outages. --- ## Quickstart > Prerequisites: **Docker Desktop** and **Python 3.10+**. ### 1. Configure ```bash cp .env.example .env ``` Generate real secrets in `.env` (never commit it): - `NCE_MASTER_KEY` — ≥32 random bytes; AES-256-GCM key for PII/credential encryption. `openssl rand -base64 32` - `NCE_API_KEY` / `NCE_ADMIN_API_KEY` / `NCE_MCP_API_KEY` — long random tokens - `NCE_MCP_NAMESPACE_ID` — a UUID pinning the stdio connection to one tenant, e.g. `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` ### 2. Bring up the full stack ```bash make up # bootstraps compose secrets, then `docker compose up -d --build` make status # container health ``` This launches the Quad-Stack (`nce-postgres`, `nce-mongo`, `nce-redis`, `nce-minio`), the cognitive model, and the application services (`worker`, `cron`, `admin`, `a2a`, `webhook-receiver`) behind Caddy, plus Jaeger. **Databases only** (when you want to run the app from your host): ```bash make local-up # docker-compose.local.yml — just Postgres, Mongo, Redis, MinIO ``` ### 3. Run from the host (optional) ```bash python -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\activate # Windows · source .venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux pip install -r requirements.txt python server.py # MCP stdio server (listens on stdin for JSON-RPC) python start_worker.py # background RQ worker (separate shell) python -m nce.cron # schedulers (separate shell) ``` ### 4. Verify ```bash make verify # runs verify_v1_launch.py end-to-end ``` --- ## Connecting an MCP Client ### Claude Desktop Edit `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows) or `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS): ```json { "mcpServers": { "nce-memory": { "command": "python", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/NCE/server.py"], "env": { "MONGO_URI": "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017", "PG_DSN": "postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@127.0.0.1:5432/memory_meta", "REDIS_URL": "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0", "MINIO_ENDPOINT": "127.0.0.1:9002", "MINIO_ACCESS_KEY": "mcp_admin", "MINIO_SECRET_KEY": "super_secure_minio_password", "NCE_MASTER_KEY": "your-32-byte-master-key", "NCE_MCP_API_KEY": "your-client-api-key", "NCE_MCP_NAMESPACE_ID": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" } } } } ``` **Cursor** — *Settings → MCP → Add New Tool*, command `python`, args `["/absolute/path/to/NCE/server.py"]`, same `env` block. A ready-to-edit template ships as [`mcp_config.json.example`](mcp_config.json.example). --- ## MCP Tool Surface Tools are dispatched through `nce/mcp_stdio_dispatch.py`, which enforces auth, quotas, and runtime enable/disable state. Highlights (`[ADMIN]` tools require `admin_api_key`): | Tool | What it does | | :--- | :--- | | `store_memory` | Persist a memory; extract entities; build KG edges (Saga write) | | `store_artifact` | Ingest media/PDF/logs into MinIO + index metadata | | `semantic_search` | Vector cosine search + Mongo hydration; optional `as_of` | | `graph_search` | GraphRAG: anchor by similarity, BFS the KG, return a subgraph; optional `as_of` | | `describe_schema` | List live entity types & edge predicates (avoid hallucinated graph constraints) | | `suggest_queries` / `execute_query_template` | Discover and run pre-optimised query templates | | `index_code_file` / `check_indexing_status` / `search_codebase` | Async AST code indexing & semantic code search | | `boost_memory` / `forget_memory` | Reinforce or zero a memory's salience | | `list_contradictions` / `resolve_contradiction` | Surface and settle logical conflicts | | `create_snapshot` / `list_snapshots` / `compare_states` | Point-in-time references & state diffing | | `replay_observe` / `replay_fork` / `replay_reconstruct` / `replay_status` | Deterministic & forked replay | | `verify_memory` / `get_event_provenance` | Integrity check & causal-chain trace | | `a2a_create_grant` · `a2a_query_shared` · `a2a_revoke_grant` · `a2a_list_grants` · … | Cross-agent federated sharing | | `connect_bridge` / `complete_bridge_auth` / `list_bridges` / `force_resync_bridge` | Document-bridge lifecycle | | `manage_namespace` · `manage_quotas` · `trigger_consolidation` · `rotate_signing_key` · `get_health` · `list_dlq` | `[ADMIN]` operations | Migration tools (`start_migration`, `validate_migration`, `commit_migration`, …) are included unless disabled, and vertical-engine tool families (`product_*`, `procurement_*`, `vendors_*`, `sales_*`, `system_design_*`, `project_*`, `d365_*`, `diag_*`, …) register when their engine is enabled. The authoritative registry is [`nce/tool_registry.py`](nce/tool_registry.py), pinned by `_EXPECTED_TOTAL` in [`tests/test_tool_registry.py`](tests/test_tool_registry.py); current per-engine and shared counts are generated in [`docs/_generated/surface.md`](docs/_generated/surface.md) and [`docs/vertical_engines/ENGINE_STATUS.md`](docs/vertical_engines/ENGINE_STATUS.md). --- ## Security Model - **Multi-tenant by construction.** Every application checkout passes through `scoped_pg_session`, which sets `SET LOCAL nce.namespace_id = ''`. All relational tables have RLS **enabled and forced**; policies validate via `get_nce_namespace()`. Privileged GC runs under a separate `BYPASSRLS` role, out of band. - **Encryption at rest.** PII, credentials, and biometric tensors are AES-256-GCM encrypted under `NCE_MASTER_KEY`. An automated PII pipeline (Presidio/regex) supports redaction and reversible pseudonymisation — see [docs/pii.md](docs/pii.md). - **Integrity & non-repudiation.** The `event_log` is append-only (a `prevent_mutation` trigger blocks edits) and hash-chained; entries are HMAC-SHA256 signed over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON, with rotatable signing keys. See [docs/signing.md](docs/signing.md). - **AuthN/Z.** HMAC-authenticated admin HTTP with optional Redis-backed replay protection; JWT (HS256 secret or RS256 public key) for A2A and protected routes; optional **mTLS** behind your edge proxy. - **A2A federation.** Sharing tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes mapped to expirations and JSONB scopes; inbound queries are scope-checked then executed bound to the *owner's* RLS namespace. Full guide: [docs/enterprise_security.md](docs/enterprise_security.md) · [docs/multi_tenancy.md](docs/multi_tenancy.md). --- ## Vertical Modules NCE ships domain verticals that turn the cognitive core into an operational tool. ### Shared-Core Foundation All business engines sit on a common cross-engine foundation (C1–C9): **entity resolution** with a merge-review queue and survivorship rules, **autonomy governance** (`@governed` confirm-first gates, value/volume ceilings, allowlists, kill switch), **external-principal RLS** scoping for partner/customer access, **allow-list field redaction**, a per-function **`d365 | both | nce` source-mode** switch with divergence logging, deterministic **pricing resolution**, a cryptographic **signing ceremony** for documents that leave the system, and **structural grounding guards** (citation-required answers, no-ranked-people rule). Guide: [docs/shared-core/overview.md](docs/shared-core/overview.md). ### Engines Per-namespace opt-in; documented under [docs/engines/](docs/engines/) (see the [docs index](docs/README.md#vertical-engine-guides)): **20 module packages** live under `nce/vertical_modules/` — 17 business engines plus the `diagnostics`, `dynamics365` and `netbox` integrations. Per-engine tool/route/core counts are measured in [`docs/vertical_engines/ENGINE_STATUS.md`](docs/vertical_engines/ENGINE_STATUS.md) and the generated [`docs/_generated/surface.md`](docs/_generated/surface.md). - **Product** — catalog search & on-demand enrichment, related-product/BOM matching, golden-record survivorship, EOL watchers. - **Procurement** — TCO calculation, supplier ranking, three-way match, and PO generation/submission behind confirm-first autonomy ceilings (real money never moves without a human). - **Agreements** — OCR → structured agreement extraction with a human review queue (money/legal terms never auto-promote), kickback reconciliation, coverage analysis. - **Vendors & Contractors** — vendor registry with scorecards (sparse data scores neutral, not bad), contractor matching & dispatch, partner-scoped views. - **Sales** — D365-mirrored lead → opportunity → quote read model, dealroom pricing via the shared pricing resolver, a **single immutable signed-baseline freeze per quote** (append-only at the database grant level), public customer quote links (HMAC-tokenised, redacted), and source-mode divergence tracking. - **System Design** — propose-only design generation with a human validation gate, device/topology capability checks, SoW generation with freeze-on-issue *(design ↔ quote round-trip planned)*. - **Project** — G0–G6 phase gates with config-as-IP criteria, signed-quote conversion (reads the Sales baseline), event-driven BOM→task sync, My-Day/capacity/scope-creep insights *(partial — some surfaces REST-only or not yet wired)*. - **Economy** — owns `INVOICE`/`POSTING`/`MARGIN`: 130-point invoice matching, NGAAP periodisation, a WORM balance trigger, the 7-effect cascade and MRR/ARR roll-ups. - **Warehouse & Inventory** — owns `STOCK_LOCATION`/`GOODS_RECEIPT`: append-only transactions, reservation algebra, row-locked decrements, kitting and restock advice. - **Assets** — owns `ASSET`/`TELEMETRY`: a 14-state lifecycle, seeding from BOM lines, SLA attachment and health scoring. - **Support** — owns `TICKET` and the SLA clock: query/open/resolve/triage, SLA clocks with a breach sweep on cron, customer-health scoring. - **Staff & Resources** — owns `RESOURCE`/`ALLOCATION`: double-booking made impossible at the database (`EXCLUDE USING gist`), capacity, travel and material-flow planning. - **Field Tech** — owns `WORK_ORDER`: work orders under dual RLS (namespace + partner scope), ISO 9001 checklists, time entries and outcome feedback. - **HR** — owns `EMPLOYEE`/`SKILL`/`CERTIFICATION`: profiles, skills matching, capacity, certification status with an expiry watcher on cron, absences and onboarding. - **Marketing** — case-study candidates and grounded drafting, anonymise-by-default, testimonials with consent tiers, AEO/GEO content. - **Business Insights** — KPI cockpit, executive morning brief with a provenance graph, cross-engine risk radar, Monte-Carlo scenarios and board pack. - **Customer Portal** — the external customer surface, owning `PORTAL_USER`/`SERVICE_REQUEST` on its own app shell, with a four-layer security spine over the C3 external-scope model. - **NetBox** — GraphQL topology activation (sites/racks/devices/cables → adjacency graph), unregistered-asset discovery against live telemetry, a do-calculus circuit-provider escalator, longitudinal **operator stress tracking** with on-call weight redistribution, and an **active-learning queue** (low-confidence memories quarantined for gamified operator review). There is also a NetBox **Cognitive Dashboard** Django plugin under `src/nce-netbox-plugin/`. - **Dynamics 365** — case enrichment with graph context, entity sync to `kg_edges`, empathic-tensor frustration/burnout reports, SLA-breach records from the WORM log, and a D365 ↔ NetBox cross-reference mapper. - **Diagnostics** — log-bundle digestion pipeline (streaming ingest, digest writer, enrichment, source profiles) surfaced through `diag_*` tools. Details: [docs/netbox_and_cognitive_extensions.md](docs/netbox_and_cognitive_extensions.md) · [docs/d365_integration_reference.md](docs/d365_integration_reference.md). --- ## Terminology: "kickback" This codebase uses the word **kickback** in its Norwegian commercial sense, where *kickback* is the ordinary term for a **volume-based supplier rebate** — a discount a supplier pays back once agreed purchase thresholds are met. It is a standard, openly negotiated clause in Nordic framework agreements and it appears on invoices, in contracts and in accounting records. **It does not mean a bribe, a secret commission, or any improper payment.** The distinction is enforced in the code, not just asserted here. In `nce/vertical_modules/agreements/compliance.py`, the clause matcher scans supplier agreements for a set of flags in which `kickback_prohibited` and `anti_bribery` are **separate entries** — a rebate clause and a bribery clause are different things, detected independently. Where the word appears, it is one of three things: | appearance | why it stays | |---|---| | Clause keywords in `compliance.py` (`no_kickback`, `kickback_prohibited`) | These are **search terms for text in third-party contracts.** A contract that literally says "no kickback" must still match. Renaming them would silently break detection. | | `procurement_kickback_tiers` | A **database table this project does not own.** It is queried defensively and degrades to empty when absent; renaming it would break the lookup against the table's real name. | | `kickback_tiers`, `do_reconcile_kickback`, `kickback_accrued` | The domain itself: reconciling accrued supplier rebates against general-ledger spend. | One thing was deliberately renamed. The supplier-**scoring** weight `kickback_proximity` is now `rebate_proximity`, because that name described *our own ranking behaviour* rather than a term in someone else's contract — "rank suppliers by kickback proximity" reads as scoring suppliers by bribe, and the project's own spec review had already flagged it as the single biggest reputational risk in the suite. The legacy key is still honoured so existing configurations keep working. The rule applied: **rename what describes our behaviour; keep and document what describes the documents we read.** ### A false friend, for the amused Norwegian and English part ways on this word. In Norwegian, a *kickback* is something you negotiate in the open, write into the contract, and reconcile against the general ledger at year end. In English, it is something you get arrested for. Same eight letters, meaningfully different consequences. It survives in this codebase for the least glamorous reason imaginable: the contracts are written in Norwegian, and a clause matcher has to look for the word the vendor actually typed. So we renamed the one place where *we* used it to describe our own behaviour, and left the rest as the false friend it is — with `anti_bribery` sitting two lines below it in the same list, quietly doing the job everyone assumes `kickback` is doing. If you are reading this because you grepped the repository for something alarming: this was the alarming thing, and it is a discount. ## Tech Stack - **Runtime** — Python 3.10+ - **Protocol** — MCP over JSON-RPC 2.0 (stdio); HTTP for admin/A2A/webhooks - **Relational + vector** — PostgreSQL 16 with `pgvector` and `pgcrypto` - **Episodic store** — MongoDB 7.0 - **Cache / queues** — Redis 7.4 (+ `rq`) - **Object storage** — MinIO (S3-compatible) - **NLP / graph** — spaCy (entities), NetworkX, HDBSCAN, cross-encoder NLI - **Code parsing** — Tree-sitter - **Validation** — Pydantic V2 - **Observability** — OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Jaeger Transitive dependencies are pinned in [`requirements.lock`](requirements.lock); regenerate with `make lockfile`. --- ## Testing & Quality Gates ```bash pytest tests/ # full suite (RLS scoping, Saga rollbacks, temporal reads, tools) pytest -m integration # integration tests (require running backing services) make lint # ruff check + ruff format --check (the CI gate) make typecheck # mypy (strict) make fmt # apply the formatter ``` --- ## Documentation The [`docs/`](docs/) tree is the source of truth. Start here: | Area | Document | | :--- | :--- | | Get running fast | [quick_start.md](docs/quick_start.md) · [developer_onboarding.md](docs/developer_onboarding.md) | | How it talks | [usage_modes.md](docs/usage_modes.md) | | Architecture | [architecture-v1.md](docs/architecture-v1.md) · [database_architecture.md](docs/database_architecture.md) | | Configuration | [configuration_reference.md](docs/configuration_reference.md) · [it_admin_guide.md](docs/it_admin_guide.md) | | Security | [enterprise_security.md](docs/enterprise_security.md) · [signing.md](docs/signing.md) · [pii.md](docs/pii.md) | | Cognition | [cognitive_layer.md](docs/cognitive_layer.md) · [llm_providers.md](docs/llm_providers.md) | | Time & simulation | [time_travel.md](docs/time_travel.md) · [replay.md](docs/replay.md) · [migrations.md](docs/migrations.md) | | Integrations | [service_integrations.md](docs/service_integrations.md) · [bridge_setup_guide.md](docs/bridge_setup_guide.md) · [a2a.md](docs/a2a.md) | | Edge | [airgapped_deployment.md](docs/airgapped_deployment.md) · [vram_monitoring.md](docs/vram_monitoring.md) | | Business engines | [shared-core/overview.md](docs/shared-core/overview.md) · [engines/](docs/engines/) | | Design decisions | [adr/](docs/adr/) | --- ## Production Checklist - Set `NCE_ENV=production`; supply strong random `NCE_API_KEY`, `NCE_ADMIN_API_KEY`, `NCE_MASTER_KEY` (≥32 bytes). - `NCE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` must be a `$pbkdf2$…` hash; set `NCE_LOAD_DOTENV=false`, `NCE_ALLOW_ADMIN_DOTENV_PERSIST=false`. - Keep guardrails on: `NCE_ADMIN_OVERRIDE=false`, `NCE_BYPASS_WORM=false`, `NCE_BYPASS_RLS=false`. - Enforce TLS everywhere (`?sslmode=require` for Postgres); prefer `NCE_ADMIN_MTLS_ENABLED=true` behind your edge proxy. - Leave the `prevent_mutation` trigger on `event_log` in place — never disable WORM. - Migration MCP tools stay disabled in prod (`NCE_DISABLE_MIGRATION_MCP=true`) outside controlled windows. - Rotate HMAC keys and JWT certificates on a schedule. --- NCE — Neuro-Cognitive Engine · v3.0.0 · © Sindre Løvlie Haugen · AGPL-3.0. Formerly TriMCP.

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Ruff lint & format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Install Ruff
        run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Ruff check
        run: ruff check .

      # TDL-4/5 (2026-06-22): the ruff format sweep + isort first-party rename (trimcp -> nce)
      # landed on main at the post-realignment sweet spot (v3.0). Now BLOCKING.
      - name: Ruff format (check only)
        run: ruff format --check .

      # TD-1: this checker existed but was wired into no workflow, so neither its
      # passes nor its failures were ever observed. Link and code-fence failures are
      # blocking; the Verified-against stamp is reported as a warning only. It needs
      # no database and no services, so it belongs in the lint job.
      - name: Docs links & code fences
        run: python scripts/verify_docs_links_and_syntax.py

      # 🔴 The generated engine figures were STALE on `main` at 3c019bd, while the page's own
      # header read "This page is generated by scripts/gen_engine_figures.py - it cannot go
      # stale." It said 271 tools / migrations 001->078; the tree held 273 and 001->080, and
      # ENGINE_STATUS.md mirrored both wrong numbers.
      #
      # The generator already shipped a --check mode (D-GEN). Nothing ran it: a grep for
      # "engine_figures" across tests/, .github/ and scripts/ matched the generator itself and
      # nothing else. A gate that exists and is wired into no workflow is the same defect class
      # as TD-1 above, and as the healthchecks that returned 200 on a degraded payload.
      #
      # Cost of this gate, stated rather than inherited: a PR that adds a tool or a migration
      # must regenerate. That is bounded - unlike the waves_landed byte-comparison (Q-17), which
      # went red on EVERY commit because wave stamps move with unrelated merges. These counters
      # move only when someone adds a counted thing, and that someone is exactly who should
      # update the page. Fix: python scripts/gen_engine_figures.py --repo . --baseline HEAD
      #   --out docs/_generated/engine_figures.md --update-status docs/vertical_engines/ENGINE_STATUS.md
      - name: Engine figures are current (D-GEN gate)
        run: |
          python scripts/gen_engine_figures.py --repo . --baseline HEAD             --out docs/_generated/engine_figures.md --check

      # Q-4 step 2. `schema.sql` is now the reviewable source; `schema_bootstrap.sql` and
      # `schema_runtime.sql` are GENERATED from it and are what connect() actually executes.
      # If someone edits schema.sql and forgets to regenerate, the running system quietly
      # stops matching the file everyone reviews -- the same failure mode as the stale
      # engine figures above, with a much worse blast radius.
      #
      # Unlike the figures generator this reads the WORKING TREE, so no `git add` ordering
      # trap.
      - name: Schema halves match schema.sql (Q-4 gate)
        run: python scripts/split_schema.py --check

      # TDL-6: was DEFERRED (continue-on-error) because pip-tools 7.4.1 crashed on the runner's
      # pip ("'PackageFinder' object has no attribute 'allow_all_prereleases'") and the lock was
      # Python-3.10-compiled while CI runs 3.11. Both fixed: pip-tools 7.6.1 + lock regenerated.
      # Now BLOCKING — a stale lock is how the aiosmtplib CVE stayed pinned after the fix landed.
      #
      # 🔴 2026-09-08: the lock was compiled under 3.11 to match THIS RUNNER, which is the wrong
      # invariant. The runtime image is python:3.12-slim-bookworm (deploy/multiuser/Dockerfile),
      # so a 3.11-resolved lock cannot represent what production installs: every distribution
      # requiring >=3.12 is invisible to it. numpy 2.5.3 and scipy 1.18.1 both declare
      # Requires-Python >=3.12, and the deployed containers run them, while a 3.11 resolve of the
      # same requirements.txt caps out at numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1. Reproducible-in-CI is not
      # the goal; representative-of-production is. Pinned to the runtime's Python below.
      #
      # Keep this in step with `.github/workflows/refresh-lock.yml` and with the Dockerfile's
      # base image. If they diverge again, the gate goes permanently red or permanently blind.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Verify requirements.lock is current
        run: |
          pip install pip-tools==7.6.1
          python scripts/compile_requirements.py
          git diff --exit-code requirements.lock

      # Nothing built an image in CI, so a base-image change or an un-installable pin
      # passed green by default -- #104/#105 bumped python 3.12->3.14 and collected nine
      # green checks having never constructed an image. A full build does not fit a
      # runner (the runtime image is ~6.3 GB before the wheel cache), so these two steps
      # gate the parts that actually broke instead.
      - name: Python platform coupling (runtime image = lock = matrix)
        run: python scripts/check_python_platform_coupling.py

      - name: Every locked pin installs on the runtime's Python
        # Metadata-only: proves each exact pin has a distribution for this Python and
        # platform, without downloading torch. Catches "this dependency cannot install
        # here", which is the failure a base-image bump actually causes.
        run: pip install --dry-run --no-deps -r requirements.lock

  test:
    name: Pytest (unit, py${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      # Wave T-3 / TDL-8: Three-tier test execution model:
      # 1. Fast unit tier (this job): Matrixed across Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12.
      #    3.10 is the declared requires-python = ">=3.10" floor (TDL-8), enforced at
      #    import/compile time. 🔴 3.12 is the CEILING and it is the one that was missing:
      #    the runtime image is python:3.12-slim-bookworm, so until 2026-09-08 the
      #    interpreter production actually runs was the ONLY one never tested. The floor
      #    had a matrix entry; the deployed version had none.
      #    Excludes integration, perf, and live-tier multi-engine scenarios.
      # 2. Integration tier: DB-backed suites against Postgres and Redis running on
      #    Python 3.11 only to avoid multiplying service container runtimes.
      # 3. Live tier: Nightly Golden Thread (I-7) against the live stack in
      #    .github/workflows/nightly-golden-thread.yml rather than in the PR path.
      #
      # Keep the top of this range equal to the Dockerfile's base image. TDL-8's original
      # failure was a declaration nothing asserted (`from datetime import UTC`, 3.11+, in
      # production code, on a green CI); testing only the floor reproduces that shape at
      # the other end of the range.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: |
            requirements.txt
            requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          # CI has no GPU. torch is pinned >=2.13.0 and floated to 2.14.0, whose
          # default wheels pull nvidia_cudnn_cu13 (553 MB), nvidia_nccl_cu13
          # (216 MB) and triton (248 MB) on top of torch itself (555 MB) -- about
          # 3.2 GB of downloads, which exhausts the runner disk (ENOSPC). The CPU
          # index drops the CUDA wheels entirely; nothing here runs on a GPU.
          pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch
          pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Pytest (exclude integration)
        env:
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          DROPBOX_APP_SECRET: test-dropbox-secret
          GRAPH_CLIENT_STATE: test-graph-state
          DRIVE_CHANNEL_TOKEN: test-drive-token
          MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: test-minio-access-key
          MINIO_SECRET_KEY: test-minio-secret-key
        # Wave T-3: Exclude integration, perf, and live-tier scenarios.
        # Golden Thread multi-engine scenario runs nightly against the live stack.
        run: pytest tests/ -m "not integration and not perf and not live" -q --tb=short

      - name: Empty with-block gate
        run: python scripts/check_empty_with.py

  security:
    name: Security & IaC validate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install security tools
        run: pip install bandit==1.8.3 pip-audit==2.9.0

      - name: Bandit (high severity)
        # --severity-level high matches this step's declared intent; -ll
        # (medium+) fails on ~80 B608 string-SQL findings in namespace-scoped
        # query builders that are individually reviewed in-wave. Medium-level
        # triage is tracked as TDL backlog, not a merge gate.
        run: bandit -r nce server.py admin_server.py --severity-level high -q

      - name: pip-audit (requirements)
        # Let pip-audit resolve the requirements in its isolated venv and
        # audit the actual resolved versions. The previous --disable-pip
        # invocation exits 2 under pip-audit 2.9.0 (CLI usage error), and
        # --no-deps additionally demands exact == pins while
        # requirements.txt deliberately uses >= ranges.
        run: pip-audit -r requirements.txt --strict

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v4
        with:
          # 1.6.0's bundled release-signing keyring has expired — provider
          # install dies with "openpgp: key expired" during init. Track
          # latest: this job only runs `terraform validate`.
          terraform_version: "latest"

      - name: Terraform validate (GCP)
        working-directory: trimcp-infra/gcp
        run: |
          terraform init -backend=false
          terraform validate

      - name: Terraform validate (AWS)
        working-directory: trimcp-infra/aws
        run: |
          terraform init -backend=false
          terraform validate

      - name: Docker Compose config validate
        env:
          # docker-compose.yml uses ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?...} required
          # interpolation; config validation only needs A value, not the
          # real secret.
          REDIS_PASSWORD: ci-config-validate-dummy
        # The env_file entries are gitignored deploy-local files — seed them
        # from the tracked example so config validation can resolve them.
        run: |
          cp deploy/compose.stack.env.example deploy/compose.stack.env
          touch deploy/compose.stack.env.generated
          docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config --quiet

  integration:
    name: Pytest (integration smoke)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: mcp_user
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: mcp_password
          POSTGRES_DB: memory_meta
        ports:
          - 15432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U mcp_user -d memory_meta"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12
      # Redis for the M6 System Design cache-invalidation tests, which need
      # Postgres AND Redis in the same job: they author through the real cores
      # (so they need the pool and namespace fixtures) and then assert the cached
      # read path serves fresh data (so they need a real Redis -- a mock stores
      # nothing and cannot detect staleness). The dedicated cache-invalidation
      # job cannot host them; it has no Postgres.
      #
      # Deliberately published on 6380, NOT the default 6379. A `services:` block
      # is job-wide, so binding the default port would put a reachable Redis
      # under every other step here and silently flip any test that currently
      # takes a Redis-absent fallback path -- the exact objection that kept the
      # cache-invalidation job separate. On 6380 the ambient default
      # (redis://localhost:6379/0) still finds nothing, and only the step that
      # sets NCE_TEST_REDIS_URL explicitly can reach it.
      redis:
        image: redis:7.4-alpine
        ports:
          - 6380:6379
          # Host ports 15432/16379 (and this 6380) are deliberately NOT the
          # service's own port. On a SELF-HOSTED runner under WSL2, Windows'
          # localhost is forwarded into the distro, so the developer stack's
          # Docker Desktop publishes of 5432/6379 are already bound and the
          # service container fails with "address already in use" before any
          # test runs. Hosted runners do not care which host port is used.
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6

          # 3.2 GB of downloads, which exhausts the runner disk (ENOSPC). The CPU

      # Waves 4 and 6 were both wired here by the ORCHESTRATOR, not by their own
      # waves. Each brief allowed a fixed file list that did not include ci.yml,
      # so both coders correctly STOPped and reported rather than widening their
      # own scope. That STOP is the intended behaviour: test_ci_integration_coverage
      # exists precisely because "written and passing locally" is not the same as
      # "gating anything", and a wave that quietly edits ci.yml to silence its own
      # ratchet is the failure this repo has already paid for twice.
      # Wave 5 (gr-match-trigger) adds the Receive->Match->Cascade keystone:
      # that a genuinely-new goods receipt fires procurement_evaluate_match
      # EXACTLY ONCE, that a replayed receipt fires it ZERO additional times
      # (idempotency inherited from goods_receipts_idempotency_uq rather than
      # re-implemented), and that a second namespace's receipts under the SAME
      # po_ref never contribute to the first's matched quantity. That last one
      # is why the namespace predicate is load-bearing here: po_ref is NOT
      # unique across tenants. The test seeds the same po_ref in two tenants
      # and reads through the OWNER pool, so the predicate is the only thing
      # separating them — through nce_app the RLS policy would refuse the leak
      # regardless and the test would prove nothing (_ORCHESTRATOR.md §6.4).
      #
      # Wired by the ORCHESTRATOR, not by the wave: Batch 133's brief allowed
      # exactly two files, so the coder correctly STOPped and reported rather
      # than silencing its own ratchet. See tests/test_ci_integration_coverage.py.
      #
      # Batch 152a switched this step from a hardcoded file list to a prefix
      # glob, so a new tests/test_inventory_*.py file needs no further ci.yml
      # edit. Verified at that rebase: the glob resolves to exactly the same 8
      # files this list named, test_inventory_match_trigger.py included.
      - name: Integration — M11 Inventory (tests/test_inventory_*.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_inventory_*.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # Module 0, Wave 31 (Batch 132a): tests/test_bom_line_store.py.
      # BOM_LINE is a Module 0 foundation object (shared across system_design
      # and sales, and read by project/procurement/inventory/economy) so this
      # file fits no per-module glob above (test_economy_*, test_inventory_*,
      # test_assets_*, test_system_design_*) — that is correct rather than a
      # naming mistake; naming it e.g. test_inventory_bom_line_store.py to
      # catch an existing glob would assert a false owner. A dedicated step,
      # added rather than folded into another module's step, is what a
      # rebase against a concurrent glob-rewrite of those other steps
      # survives. See tests/test_ci_integration_coverage.py.
      - name: Integration — M0 BOM_LINE store (tests/test_bom_line_store.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_bom_line_store.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # Lane F Wave F-11: tests/test_geodata_osm.py -- box/GiST bbox-query and
      # ON CONFLICT upsert behaviour against the real geodata_osm_elements
      # global table, which no mock can prove. A dedicated step rather than a
      # test_geodata_*.py glob (two geodata integration files exist as of
      # Wave F-12 below; a glob covering both is a later step, not this
      # one's job to introduce). Flagged by ML-orch (2026-09-18): these
      # tests carried @pytest.mark.integration but ran in no workflow, so they
      # gated nothing.
      - name: Integration — geodata OSM elements (tests/test_geodata_osm.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_geodata_osm.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # Lane F Wave F-12: tests/test_geodata_n50.py -- same reasoning as
      # F-11's geodata OSM step above, against the real geodata_n50_land_cover
      # global table.
      - name: Integration — geodata N50 land cover (tests/test_geodata_n50.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_geodata_n50.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # Lane F Wave F-13: tests/test_geodata_place_names.py -- point/GiST
      # nearest-neighbour lookup and ON CONFLICT upsert behaviour against the
      # real geodata_place_names global table, which no mock can prove. Same
      # reasoning as F-11's geodata OSM step above.
      - name: Integration — geodata place names (tests/test_geodata_place_names.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_geodata_place_names.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # Module 5, Wave 15 (Batch 132d): tests/test_sales_lines_manual.py -- the
      # MANUAL-PICK origination path for BOM_LINE, and the first real caller of
      # the guarded store above. There is no test_sales_* glob in this workflow
      # (the globs are test_economy_*, test_inventory_*, test_assets_* and
      # test_system_design_*; Sales appears only as one hardcoded filename in
      # the smoke step), so without this step the file would run in NO job --
      # exactly what tests/test_ci_integration_coverage.py exists to catch.
      # A DEDICATED step, added rather than folded into another module's, is
      # what survives a rebase against a concurrent glob rewrite; renaming the
      # file to sneak under an existing glob would assert a false owner.
      # What it gates: that a guarded write actually reaches bom_line_content
      # with origin_kind='manual'/writer_engine='sales', that the deny path
      # still fires (unregistered transition AND wrong engine), that a
      # caller-supplied origin_kind cannot reach the store, and idempotency on
      # bom_line_label. Downstream waves seed BOM_LINE rows by raw SQL, which
      # bypasses assert_owner entirely -- this step is what makes those mean
      # something.
      # Tenant-isolation predicates: five queries that sat inside a namespace-scoped
      # session but omitted the namespace from their WHERE clause. The fixture collides
      # every identifier across two namespaces and differentiates only on content, so it
      # FAILS if any predicate is removed -- that is the whole point of the file, and it
      # gates nothing unless a job runs it (see tests/test_ci_integration_coverage.py).
      # Needs Postgres only: the file declares its own tp_pool fixture rather than
      # conftest's pg_pool, because none of the five queries touch signing.
      - name: Integration — tenant-isolation predicates
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
        run: pytest tests/test_tenant_predicates.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      - name: Integration — M5 Sales BOM_LINE origination + read seam
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        # tests/test_sales_dealroom.py carries the D53 regression cover (unpriced
        # vs UNDATED vs price_resolution_failed) and ran in NO job until D55.
        # One of its nine tests boots a real NCEEngine via engine.connect(), which
        # needs Mongo AND MinIO; this job provides only Postgres and there is no
        # MinIO service anywhere in this workflow. That ONE test is deselected by
        # name -- deliberately not by adding the whole FILE back to KNOWN_UNWIRED,
        # which would have kept all nine ungated to avoid running eight of them.
        run: >-
          pytest tests/test_sales_lines_manual.py tests/test_sales_get_quote_lines.py
          tests/test_sales_dealroom.py -m integration -q --tb=short
          --deselect 'tests/test_sales_dealroom.py::TestSalesDealRoom::test_open_dealroom_prices_correctly_and_handles_toggles'

      # M9 Assets (tests/test_assets_*.py). FIRST integration job for Module 9;
      # Wave 1 (Batch 141) was a pure state machine with no DB surface to
      # integrate against. Proves FORCE RLS on `assets` via a real nce_app
      # connection — that a second namespace can neither read nor reach the
      # first's asset row — that nce_app's grant deliberately EXCLUDES DELETE,
      # and that do_seed_asset_from_bom is idempotent by the
      # assets_ns_bom_line_uq constraint rather than by a Python check-then-write
      # that would race. None of that is provable from the unit job, which
      # selects `-m "not integration and not perf"`: the owner/superuser pool
      # BYPASSES FORCE RLS, so an isolation test that does not use a real
      # nce_app connection passes while the query leaks in production.
      #
      # A second wave (Batch 142b) adds the Contract-A half: that an ASSET
      # kg_node write is REFUSED when the node-ownership.json row is absent and
      # PERMITTED when it is present — deny-by-default proven in both
      # directions, not just the happy path — and that the projection is
      # idempotent under re-run. Its namespace-scoping test seeds the SAME
      # asset_id in two tenants and reads through the OWNER pool, so the
      # namespace predicate is the only thing separating them; through nce_app
      # the RLS policy would refuse the leak regardless and the test would
      # prove nothing (see _ORCHESTRATOR.md §6.4).
      #
      # Both files were wired by the ORCHESTRATOR, not by their waves. Batch
      # 142's brief allowed four files and 142b's allowed three; ci.yml was
      # outside both, so each coder correctly STOPped and reported rather than
      # silencing its own ratchet. Batch 152a switched this step from a
      # hardcoded file list to a prefix glob, so a third tests/test_assets_*.py
      # file needs no further ci.yml edit. See tests/test_ci_integration_coverage.py.
      - name: Integration — M9 Assets (tests/test_assets_*.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_assets_*.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # M6 System Design. Module 6's FIRST integration job: it had no step
      # here at all, so all eight of its DB-backed files sat in KNOWN_UNWIRED
      # and gated nothing (§9.9). This wave ran all eight against a real
      # Postgres before wiring them — 58 marked tests, all green — and removed
      # all eight KNOWN_UNWIRED entries.
      #
      # Wired as a per-module glob (§7.9, the B152a pattern) so the nine M6
      # waves queued behind this one each land a DB-backed test with ZERO
      # further ci.yml edits — the undeclared-chokepoint defect this shape
      # exists to stop.
      #
      # The glob is non-recursive, so it does NOT reach the five pure-unit
      # System Design files under tests/unit/ (lucid, sharepoint, skeleton,
      # sow, toolcount). None of those carries an integration marker or needs
      # a database, so they stay in the unit job — which is why none of them
      # needs a GLOBBED_UNMARKED_BY_DESIGN entry. Falsify that by resolving
      # the glob: it yields exactly the eight top-level files, every one
      # marked.
      #
      # NB: the ratchet's token scanner reads this whole file, comments
      # included, so spelling any other test-path glob in a comment here
      # registers it as a wired CI glob and breaks the ratchets. Name paths
      # in prose, not as patterns.
      - name: Integration — M6 System Design (tests/test_system_design_*.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
          # Points at the 6380 service above. Without it the cache-invalidation
          # tests skip, and a skipped gate gates nothing.
          NCE_TEST_REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6380/14
        run: pytest tests/test_system_design_*.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # M10 Support Engine (Module 10, Wave 8). Proves Contract-H native Support
      # tenant isolation, SLA clocks, customer health, and Contract-A node ownership.
      - name: Integration — M10 Support Engine (tests/test_support_hardening.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_support_hardening.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # M12 Field Tech Engine (Module 12, Wave 8). Proves work order lifecycle,
      # tenant isolation, ISO9001 checklists, offline sync, and Contract-A node ownership.
      - name: Integration — M12 Field Tech Engine (tests/test_field_tech_hardening.py)
        env:

      - name: Integration — M14 Marketing Engine (tests/test_marketing_*.py)

      - name: Integration — M15 Staff & Resources Engine (tests/test_resources_*.py)

          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_resources_*.py -m integration -q --tb=short

      # board pack draft staging, tenant isolation on business_insights_kpi_snapshots,

      # BI-3 third-party egress boundary, BI-4 grace degradation).
      - name: Integration — M16 Business Insights Engine (tests/test_business_insights_*.py)
        env:
          PG_DSN: postgresql://mcp_user:mcp_password@localhost:15432/memory_meta
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_INTEGRATION_REFRESH_SIGNING_ON_DECRYPT_FAIL: "1"
        run: pytest tests/test_business_insights_*.py -m integration -q --tb=short



  # REST-surface mutations must invalidate the MCP response cache.
  # `bump_cache_generation` is called from the MCP dispatch loop only, so a
  # mutation performed through nce/admin_handlers/* left cacheable MCP reads
  # serving pre-mutation data for the full MCP_CACHE_TTL_S (300 s). Found in the
  # Batch 143 audit; pre-existing and systemic, not introduced by that wave.
  #
  # This runs as its OWN job rather than a step in `integration`, for two
  # reasons. It needs a real Redis — tests/test_mcp_cache.py mocks
  # redis_client, which stores nothing and therefore cannot detect staleness at
  # all — and a `services:` block is job-wide, so adding Redis to `integration`
  # would put a live Redis under every other step there, silently flipping any
  # test that currently takes a Redis-absent fallback path. It also needs no
  # Postgres: the test stubs the do_* cores and exercises the cache mechanism
  # itself, so a dedicated job is both safer and cheaper.
  cache-invalidation:
    name: Pytest (REST/MCP cache invalidation)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7.4-alpine
        ports:
          - 16379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: |
            requirements.txt
            requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          # CI has no GPU. torch is pinned >=2.13.0 and floated to 2.14.0, whose
          # default wheels pull nvidia_cudnn_cu13 (553 MB), nvidia_nccl_cu13
          # (216 MB) and triton (248 MB) on top of torch itself (555 MB) -- about
          # 3.2 GB of downloads, which exhausts the runner disk (ENOSPC). The CPU
          # index drops the CUDA wheels entirely; nothing here runs on a GPU.
          pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch
          pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt

      # Reads through the cacheable MCP path, mutates through the REST route,
      # reads again. FAILS on the unfixed tree — that is the point.
      - name: Integration — REST/MCP cache invalidation (real Redis)
        env:
          NCE_MASTER_KEY: ci-test-master-key-32chars-minimum!!
          NCE_TEST_REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:16379/15
        run: pytest tests/test_rest_cache_invalidation.py -m integration -q --tb=short

  go:
    name: Go (build & test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: "1.22"
          cache-dependency-path: go/go.sum

      - name: Go format check
        working-directory: ./go
        run: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"

      - name: Go vet
        working-directory: ./go
        run: go vet ./...

      - name: Go build
        working-directory: ./go
        run: go build ./...

      - name: Go test
        working-directory: ./go
        run: go test ./... -v

      - name: Build Linux binaries (amd64 + arm64)
        run: bash build/linux/build.sh
